```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We construct graph and conformal deformations of trapped initial-data exteriors in three and four spatial dimensions. The resulting metrics have nonnegative scalar curvature, strictly negative inner mean curvature, a lower bound protecting every enclosing cut, and an arbitrarily small upper error in ADM energy. We also give a direct four-dimensional maximal vacuum construction that retains a noncompact decaying second fundamental form. These constructions give boundary routes to the corresponding numerical Penrose inequalities.",
```

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We construct graph and conformal deformations of trapped initial-data exteriors in three and four spatial dimensions. The resulting metrics have nonnegative scalar curvature, strictly negative inner mean curvature, a lower bound protecting every enclosing cut, and an arbitrarily small upper error in ADM energy. We also give a direct four-dimensional maximal vacuum construction that retains a noncompact decaying second fundamental form. These constructions give boundary routes to the corresponding numerical Penrose inequalities.

- **claim-n3-boundary-deformation** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-prepared-output)): For every prepared exterior $(\Omega_0,g,K)$ there is a connected one-ended subexterior $\Omega\subset\Omega_0$ whose smooth compact boundary $B$ separates $S_0$ from infinity, with the following property. For each sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $N$, there is a smooth metric $\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}$ on $\overline\Omega$, complete with its boundary included, for which $$\begin{aligned} R_{\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}}&\ge0, &H_{\partial\Omega}(\widehat g_{\epsilon,N})&<0, \label{n3:prepared:curvature}\\ \widehat g_{\epsilon,N}&\ge e^{-4\epsilon}g, &E_{\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}}&\le E+\eta_{\epsilon,N}, \label{n3:prepared:comparison} \end{aligned}$$ where the boundary normal points into $\Omega$ and, at fixed $\epsilon$, $\eta_{\epsilon,N}\to0$. More precisely, for constants $C,a$ depending on the fixed data and $\epsilon$, $$0\le\eta_{\epsilon,N}\le C(1+N)^a\bigl(e^{-\epsilon N}+e^{-\epsilon N/2}\bigr).$$ The new end has $\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}-\delta=O_2(r^{-1})$ and $R_{\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}}=O(r^{-3-\delta'})$ for some $\delta'>0$. Every full enclosing cut $T$ in $\Omega$ satisfies $$\|T\|_{\widehat g_{\epsilon,N}}\ge e^{-4\epsilon}A_*.$$
  - Explanation: A prepared exterior admits a subexterior and smooth complete metrics with nonnegative scalar curvature, negative inner mean curvature, a lower metric bound protecting every enclosing cut and an arbitrarily small upper energy error.
- **claim-n3-exterior-penrose** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-inequality)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ be an exterior as in Definition <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-class">1</a>. Assume Equations <a href="#n3:intro:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:constraints">[n3:intro:constraints]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:decay">[n3:intro:decay]</a>, integrability of $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$, and the finite ADM limits <a href="#n3:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:energy">[n3:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:momentum">[n3:intro:momentum]</a>. Orient $\partial\Omega$ by the normal into $\Omega$, and suppose $\theta_+(\partial\Omega)\le0$. If $E>\|P\|_\delta$, then $$\label{n3:intro:penrose} \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2} \ge \sqrt{\frac{a_g(\partial\Omega)}{16\pi}}.$$ No extension of the data across $\partial\Omega$ is required.
  - Explanation: Invariant ADM mass is bounded below by the square root of the enclosing-area infimum over sixteen pi, for exteriors with weakly trapped boundary.
- **claim-n3-mots-barriers** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-region-theorem)): Let $(N,g,Q)$ be a smooth compact three-dimensional initial data set with boundary $\Gamma_-\sqcup\Gamma_+$. Assume $\Gamma_+$ is nonempty and has positive expansion with its normal out of $N$. The inner part $\Gamma_-$ may be empty; when it is present, assume its expansion is negative with its normal into $N$.* *Consider all smooth domains whose inner boundary is $\Gamma_-$ and whose remaining boundary $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of $N$ and satisfies $\Theta_Q(\Sigma)\leq0$. They avoid $\Gamma_+$, and their normal on $\Sigma$ points out of the domain. If their union is nonempty, its closure has a smooth compact embedded stable MOTS frontier in the interior, separating it from $\Gamma_+$. This closure is itself the closure of such a domain and contains every domain in the defining class. If $\Gamma_-$ is nonempty, the two strict barriers also give a nonempty smooth embedded enclosing MOTS.
  - Explanation: Between a negative inner and a positive outer barrier, the closure of the union of trapped domains has a smooth stable MOTS frontier.
- **claim-n3-right-continuity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-right-continuity)): Let $E_c$, $c$ in an interval, be an increasing family of closed subsets of a fixed compact metric space. Outside a countable set of parameters, $$\label{n3:domains:hausdorff-right} E_{c_j}\longrightarrow E_c\quad\hbox{in Hausdorff distance whenever} \quad c_j\downarrow c.$$ Here continuity at $E_c=\varnothing$ means that $E_{c'}$ is empty for every sufficiently close $c'>c$.
  - Explanation: An increasing family of closed sets is right-continuous in Hausdorff distance outside a countable set of parameters.
- **claim-n3-stable-collar** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-stable-collar)): Let $(N^d,g)$ be smooth, with $d\in\{3,4\}$ and a fixed smooth symmetric tensor $Q$. Let $\Sigma$ be a compact connected smooth two-sided hypersurface without boundary, forming a component of the frontier of a closed region $D$, with normal pointing out of $D$. Assume $\Theta_Q(\Sigma)=c$ and stability for outward variations. Assume also local *outward-replacement maximality*: in some collar of $\Sigma$ disjoint from the other frontier components and all designated barrier faces, no positive outward normal graph can replace $\Sigma$, leaving $D$ unchanged outside that collar, and have expansion at most $c$ everywhere on the new component. There is a smooth foliation $\Sigma_s$, $0\leq s<s_0$, of an outward collar, with $\Sigma_0=\Sigma$ and positive outward normal velocity, such that $$\label{n3:domains:collar-expansion} \Theta_Q(\Sigma_s)>c\quad(0<s<s_0),\qquad \Theta_Q(\Sigma_0)=c.$$ In particular its leaf parameter $s$ is a smooth defining function and $\|\nabla s\|$ is bounded above and below by positive constants.
  - Explanation: A maximal stable frontier carries an outward foliated collar whose leaves have expansion strictly above the threshold.
- **claim-n3-parallel-support** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-parallel-support)): Let $(N^d,g,Q)$ be smooth, with $d\in\{3,4\}$. Suppose the frontier of a closed set $D$ lies in a fixed compact interior region and has exterior-support expansion at most $c$. Put $D_z=\{y:\operatorname{dist}(y,D)\leq z\}$. For sufficiently small $z>0$, all exterior supports of $D_z$ have expansion at most $$\label{n3:domains:parallel-estimate} c+Cz.$$ The allowable radius and $C$ depend only on the compact ambient geometry and $Q$, and not on the support, its second fundamental form, or the regularity of $D$.
  - Explanation: Parallel neighborhoods keep the support expansion bound up to an additive error linear in the distance, independent of support curvature.
- **claim-n3-weak-support-enclosure** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-weak-support)): Let $N$ be a smooth compact connected three-manifold with boundary $\Gamma_-\sqcup\Gamma_+$, where $\Gamma_+$ is nonempty and $\Gamma_-$ may be empty. Let $D$ be a nonempty closed subset which contains a relative collar of $\Gamma_-$ when that boundary is prescribed, and stays a positive distance from $\Gamma_+$. Suppose its interior frontier has exterior-support expansion at most $c$ for a smooth tensor $Q$.* *For every $c'>c$ such that $\Theta_Q(\Gamma_+)>c'$ with its normal out of $N$, there is a smooth bounding domain $E$ containing $D$ in its relative interior, containing the required inner collar, and avoiding $\Gamma_+$, whose free boundary satisfies $$\label{n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion} \Theta_Q(\partial E\setminus\Gamma_-)=c'.$$ Its boundary and the domain may be disconnected. In particular $D$ is contained in the closed total trapped region at any such larger threshold. No regularity or positive-thickness assumption on $D$ is required.
  - Explanation: A closed set with weak exterior-support expansion bound lies inside a smooth domain with constant prescribed expansion.
- **claim-n3-prepared-domain** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain)): The thresholds and the domain above can be chosen with the following properties. The numbers $c_b,c_w<0$ are right-continuity points of their respective full maximal-region families. The boundary of $\Omega$ consists of the faces in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:face-expansions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:face-expansions">[n3:domains:face-expansions]</a>, has disjoint smooth outward leaf collars as in Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:stable-collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:stable-collar">7</a>, and preserves the enclosing-area lower bound in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:inherited-area" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:inherited-area">[n3:domains:inherited-area]</a>.* *There are a smooth compactly supported function $C$ on $\Omega$, constants $C_b\geq0$, $C_w\leq0$, and positive constants $k_B$ on its face collars such that $$\label{n3:domains:offset-collars} \begin{aligned} C_w\leq C\leq C_b,&\qquad C=C_b-k_Bs&&\text{in a black collar near }B_b,\\ &\qquad C=C_w+k_Bs&&\text{in a white collar near }B_w. \end{aligned}$$ For an absent type, its corresponding constant is simply a bound. Set $$\label{n3:domains:assigned-heights} b_-=c_b-C_b<0, \qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0.$$ There is a smooth positive function $\rho$, equal to a positive constant times $r^{-4}$ on the far end and satisfying symbol derivative bounds there, such that, for every $h\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$\label{n3:domains:offset-smallness} \|(h+C)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K\|+\|\nabla C\|+\rho \leq\tfrac12\mathfrak m \quad\hbox{everywhere on }\Omega.$$ The thresholds, collars, offset, and $\rho$ are fixed before the deformation parameters are chosen. After fixing the thresholds and collars, the offset and its first derivatives can be made arbitrarily small.
  - Explanation: Thresholds, domain, collars, offset and weight can be fixed so that the offset smallness holds against the constraint margin.
- **claim-n3-deformation-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-identity)): Let $f,t$ be smooth and $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}(K+H^f)$. At $\sigma>0$ decompose $S$ relative to $\mathbb Re\oplus e^\perp$: $$T=S\|_{e^\perp\times e^\perp},\quad M=S(e,\cdot)\|_{e^\perp},\quad q=S(e,e),\quad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}T=F-\chi q.$$ Then $$\label{n3:deformation:scalar-identity} \begin{split} \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g} ={}&8\pi(\mu+J(w))+\mathcal T +w(F)-F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V, \end{split}$$ where $$\label{n3:deformation:quadratic-term} \begin{split} \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12\|T^{\operatorname{tf}}\|^2 +(M+pa\nabla_\perp t)\cdot(M+(p+2)a\nabla_\perp t)\\ &+4(p+1)\|\,\mathrm dt\|_{A_d}^2 +(\chi-\chi^2/4)q^2+2(p+1)\chi qa\,\partial_e t\\ &-\chi Fq/2+3F^2/4. \end{split}$$ After substituting $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}S$, this expression extends smoothly across $\sigma=0$.
  - Explanation: The scalar curvature of the warped graph metric splits into constraint densities, a quadratic term and a divergence.
- **claim-n3-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity)): The weighted coercivity theorem of (OpenAI 2026b, Proposition 4.2) [[NumericalCompanion](#ref-NumericalCompanion)], with Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary">[n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary]</a>, makes $\mathcal T$ nonnegative. For $0\le p\le N$, $$\label{n3:deformation:coercive-estimate} \|\,\mathrm dt\|_{A_d}^2+\|T\|^2+\|M\|^2+dq^2+F^2 \le C(1+N)^A\mathcal T$$ with universal $C,A$. At $\,\mathrm dt=0$ there is the stronger comparison, uniform in $p,d$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-norm} c\bigl(\|T^{\operatorname{tf}}\|^2+\|M\|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr) \le\mathcal T \le C\bigl(\|T^{\operatorname{tf}}\|^2+\|M\|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr).$$
  - Explanation: The quadratic term is nonnegative and controls the deformation variables with polynomial constants.
- **claim-n3-boundary-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity)): On a face where $f$ is constant, $$\label{n3:deformation:boundary} V_\nu/u=d(H+4\partial_\nu t)-H+w_\nu(F-P_B).$$ Its mean curvature in $\hat g$, with normal into $\Omega$, is $e^{-2t}\sqrt d\,(H+4\partial_\nu t)$.
  - Explanation: On a face where the height is constant, the flux and the deformed mean curvature are given by explicit identities.
- **claim-n3-homotopy** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy)): There is a continuous piecewise smooth family of systems indexed by $s\in[0,4]$, beginning at <a href="#n3:deformation:trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:trace">[n3:deformation:trace]</a>, <a href="#n3:deformation:original-second-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:original-second-equation">[n3:deformation:original-second-equation]</a> and the original Dirichlet values, and ending at $f=0$ and the scalar problem with zero source and zero inner conormal flux. Throughout its first three stages the source is <a href="#n3:deformation:source" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:source">[n3:deformation:source]</a>, with $\mathcal T$ evaluated using the actual trace $F$. Each trace equation has right-side derivative at least one in $h$, with $x,Z,\nabla f$ fixed.
  - Explanation: A continuous piecewise smooth four-stage family connects the original system to a trivial scalar problem.
- **claim-n3-height-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-height)): Every smooth trace solution in Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a> satisfies $\|h\|\le C_0$, independently of $N,R$, the homotopy parameter, and the input $Z$. Its actual right side satisfies $\|F\|\le C_F$ with the same independence.
  - Explanation: Scaled height and trace right side are bounded independently of the parameters.
- **claim-n3-end-height** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-end-height)): There are $r_0,C>0$, independent of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameter, such that for $R\ge2r_0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:end-height-estimate} \|h\|\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R^{-\gamma})\quad(r_0\le r\le R).$$ In particular, $$\label{n3:deformation:outer-gradient} \|\nabla f\|\le C R^{-1-\gamma}/\tau\quad\hbox{on }S_R.$$ For fixed $\epsilon,N$, a sufficiently large lower bound for $R$ gives $t>-\epsilon$ on $S_R$.
  - Explanation: Height decays on the end and the outer gradient is controlled.
- **claim-n3-floor-curvature** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature)): At an interior point where $\,\mathrm dt=0$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}t\ge0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-gauss} \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g} \le \tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)+\mathcal S(H^f),$$ where, for a symmetric tensor $A$, $$\label{n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic} \begin{split} \mathcal S(A)={}&\tfrac14(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A)^2 -\tfrac12\|A_{\perp\perp}^{\operatorname{tf}}\|^2\\ &+dA_{ee}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A-d\|A_{e\perp}\|^2. \end{split}$$ There are universal $c_*,\eta_*>0$ and polynomial constants $C_N$ such that, at $\,\mathrm dt=0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general} \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f) \ge c_*\mathcal T-C_N(F^2+\|K\|^2).$$ If $K=0$, the more useful uniform estimate is $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end} \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)\ge c_*\mathcal T-C_N vF^2.$$
  - Explanation: At a minimum of the conformal variable, scalar curvature is compared with a Gauss-type quadratic form.
- **claim-n3-floor-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors)): There is a fixed compact set $\mathcal K\subset\overline\Omega$ containing the supports of $K,C,b,D_0,D_1$ such that, at an interior minimum $t=-\epsilon$ of a smooth solution in the first three stages, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower} \mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda/u \ge 2\delta_0\mathcal T+\tau a\sigma -C(1+N)^A [\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+v(\rho_0+\rho_1)].$$ Here $\delta_0>0$ can be fixed sufficiently small independently of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameter.
  - Explanation: At a floor contact the divergence has a lower bound with error confined to a compact set and weights.
- **claim-n3-floor-exclusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-deformation-floor)): Choose $\delta_0$ as in Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-errors" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-errors">19</a>. There is a polynomial choice $C_N=C(1+N)^A$ in the penalty such that, for all sufficiently large $N$ and all $R\ge R_{\mathrm{floor}}(N,\epsilon)$, no smooth solution anywhere along Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a> can satisfy $t\ge-\epsilon$ and attain $t=-\epsilon$. In particular every such admissible solution has $t>-\epsilon$ on $\overline{\Omega_R}$.
  - Explanation: For a suitable penalty no solution along the homotopy touches the conformal floor.
- **claim-n3-sublevel-support** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-sublevel-support)): Let $U$ be an open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$, let $Q$ be a smooth symmetric tensor on $U$, and let $u:U\to\mathbb R$ be finite and lower semicontinuous. Fix $k<k'$ and $q_0\in\mathbb R$. A smooth lower test of $u$ at $x$ is a smooth function $\phi$ with $\phi(x)=u(x)$ and $\phi\le u$ near $x$. Suppose every such test with $u(x)<k'$ and $\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$ satisfies $$\mathcal E_Q[\phi](x)\le q_0,$$ where $\mathcal E_Q$ is the expansion in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:test-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:test-expansion">[n3:domains:test-expansion]</a> of the regular level through $x$, oriented toward increasing $\phi$. Equivalently, subtract $\phi(x)$ before applying that formula. Then every smooth exterior support of the relatively closed set $D_k=\{x\in U:u(x)\le k\}$, at a frontier point in $U$, has expansion at most $q_0$.
  - Explanation: Expansion bounds on lower tests of a semicontinuous function transfer to exterior supports of its closed sublevels.
- **claim-n3-wrong-height-separation** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels)): In the first two homotopy stages, the following holds. If $Q\subset\bar\Omega$ is compact and disjoint from $\mathcal B_{c_b}$, there are $\eta_Q>0$ and $N_Q$ such that $$h\ge b_-+\eta_Q\quad\hbox{on }Q \label{n3:apriori:lower-height}$$ for every $N\ge N_Q$, every sufficiently large allowed truncation, and every admissible or floor-contact solution in those stages. If $Q$ is disjoint from $\mathcal W_{c_w}$, the analogous conclusion is $h\le b_+-\eta_Q$. The compact sets are relative to the full closure: they may contain faces of the opposite color.
  - Explanation: On compact sets away from a trapped region the height stays uniformly away from the wrong boundary height.
- **claim-n3-boundary-slopes** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-collars)): There are fixed constants $c,C_*>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $N$ and the allowed truncations, the first two stages satisfy $$\begin{array}{ll} c/\tau\le\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on black faces},\\[2pt] c/\tau\le-\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on white faces}. \end{array} \label{n3:apriori:signed-slopes}$$ During the third stage one still has $\|\partial_\nu f\|\le C_*/\tau$. On every fixed compact region needed for the final scalar-curvature estimate, the first two stages satisfy $b_-\le h\le b_+$.
  - Explanation: Signed normal slopes on black and white faces are bounded above and below by multiples of the inverse scale.
- **claim-n3-collar-traces** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-trace)): In the first two stages let $\mathcal C$ be a fixed union of disjoint collars of the inner faces, shortened if necessary. For every nonnegative smooth function $\varphi$ supported in those collars, $$\begin{aligned} \int_B L\varphi\,\mathrm dA_g &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C}u \bigl[(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi +\|d\varphi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr]\,\mathrm dV_g, \label{n3:apriori:weighted-trace}\\ \int_B\varphi\,\mathrm dA_g &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C}\sqrt D \bigl[(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi +\|d\varphi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr]\,\mathrm dV_g. \label{n3:apriori:unweighted-trace} \end{aligned}$$ The estimates also hold without a support condition on $\varphi$ if the right sides include a fixed collar cutoff equal to one on $B$, with its derivative included in the coefficient of $\varphi$.
  - Explanation: Boundary integrals are bounded by collar integrals with polynomial constants.
- **claim-n3-graph-sobolev** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-sobolev)): For a smooth function $\omega$ supported over a fixed compact base patch, which may meet an inner face, $$\\|\omega\\|_{L^6(\,\mathrm d\Gamma)}^2 \le C(N)\int_\Gamma \left[\|\nabla_\Gamma\omega\|^2+ (1+\mathcal T)\omega^2\right]\,\mathrm d\Gamma. \label{n3:apriori:sobolev-equation}$$
  - Explanation: A local Sobolev inequality holds on the ordinary graph.
- **claim-n3-bounds-before-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-apriori-bounds)): Fix the prepared data and $\epsilon>0$. There are $N_0$ and $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$ such that, for each fixed $N\ge N_0$ and every $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$, all smooth solutions of the four-stage homotopy with $t\ge-\epsilon$ satisfy $$\|h\|\le C_0,\qquad \|f\|\le C_0/\tau,\qquad -\epsilon\le t\le Z\le C(N),\qquad \|\nabla f\|\le C(N). \label{n3:apriori:bounded-variables}$$ The constants are uniform in $R$ and in the homotopy parameter. They include putative floor-contact solutions, which are then excluded by Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor">20</a>. The fixed signed slopes, the third-stage upper slopes, and the polynomial trace estimates are those of Lemmas <a href="#n3:apriori:collars" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:collars">23</a> and <a href="#n3:apriori:trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:trace">24</a>.
  - Explanation: Height, conformal variable and gradient are bounded uniformly in the radius and homotopy parameter.
- **claim-n3-axial-gradient** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-existence-gradient)): Let $U'$ be compactly contained in an interior or boundary coordinate patch $U$ in dimension three. In a boundary patch assume that $z$ is constant on the boundary face. Suppose $z$ is $C^3$, up to that face when present, $\|\nabla z\|\le L$, and, almost everywhere, $$\label{n3:existence:axial-equation} A_\chi:\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}z=G,\qquad A_\chi=I-(1-\chi)e\otimes e,\qquad e=\frac{\nabla z}{\|\nabla z\|},\qquad 0<\chi_0\le\chi\le1,$$ where $\\|G\\|_\infty\le Q$. At zero gradients any measurable unit axis for which the equation holds is allowed. Then there are $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on $\chi_0$, the patch geometry and the separation of $U'$ from the other patch boundaries, such that $$\label{n3:existence:gradient-estimate} \\|\nabla z\\|_{C^{0,\alpha}(U')} \le C(L+Q).$$ For all sufficiently small coordinate balls centered in $U'$, with intersection with the domain understood at a boundary, one also has $$\label{n3:existence:hessian-morrey} \int_{B_r\cap U}\|\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}z\|^2\,\mathrm dV_g \le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\alpha}.$$ In particular, the constants are independent of continuity moduli of $\chi$ and $G$.
  - Explanation: Solutions of the axial equation have Holder gradient and a Morrey bound on the Hessian.
- **claim-natural-growth** (theorem, [source](#stmt-b-lem-natural-growth)): Let $n\in\{3,4\}$ and let $Z\in L^\infty\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on a ball in $\mathbb R^n$. Fix a Borel representative with $\|Z\|\le M$ for products with measures. Suppose, in distributions, that $$\label{n3:existence:natural-equation} \operatorname{div}(aDZ+b)=e,$$ where $a$ is measurable and symmetric, $\lambda I\le a\le\Lambda I$ for $0<\lambda\le\Lambda$, $\|b\|\le B$, and $e$ is a signed measure satisfying $$\label{n3:existence:natural-source} \|e\|\le C_0(1+\|DZ\|^2)\,\mathrm dx+\mu,\qquad \mu(B_r(x))\le C_\mu r^{n-2+\beta},\qquad \beta>0.$$ Here $\mu$ is a positive measure, and its bound holds at every center and all sufficiently small radii in a larger patch. Assume the weak exponential product rule <a href="#n3:existence:exponential-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:existence:exponential-identity">[n3:existence:exponential-identity]</a> below is valid with the specified representative. This is true, in particular, for a function continuous across a flat interface and smooth on its two closed sides, when the equation includes the normal-flux jump. Then the Sobolev class of $Z$ has a Hölder representative on smaller balls, with constants depending only on the displayed bounds and patch separation. If $Z$ is already continuous, this is a uniform estimate for that function. The conclusion applies up to a smooth face whenever its reflected equation satisfies these hypotheses.
  - Explanation: A bounded solution with quadratic gradient growth and a measure source has a Holder representative.
- **claim-n3-classical-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-existence-classical-bounds)): Fix the deformation parameters and assume the bounds in Proposition <a href="#n3:apriori:bounds" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:bounds">26</a>. Every smooth solution in the homotopy of Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a>, with $t\ge-\epsilon$, has uniform local classical estimates of every finite order, up to the inner and outer faces. At fixed $N$ the constants are independent of the homotopy parameter and of all sufficiently large outer radii $R$. The local patches can be chosen with a uniform positive radius throughout the end.
  - Explanation: Bounded-variable solutions have classical estimates of every finite order.
- **claim-n3-scalar-solve** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-existence-scalar-solve)): Fix $N\ge4$, $\tau>0$, a finite smooth truncation $\Omega_R$, and a homotopy parameter $s\in[0,4]$. For every $Z\in C^{1,b}(\overline{\Omega_R})$, $0<b<1$, the scalar trace equation of Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a>, with its prescribed componentwise constant Dirichlet values for $f$, has a unique solution. It lies in $C^{3,b}$ and is smooth to the extent allowed by the input. The solution operator $$\label{n3:existence:scalar-operator} f=\mathcal S_s(Z)$$ is continuous in $(s,Z)$, including across the concatenation points of the homotopy. On bounded subsets of $C^{1,b}$ its $C^{3,b}$ norm is uniformly bounded at these fixed parameters. No lower bound for $t$ is required.
  - Explanation: The scalar trace equation is uniquely solvable for every trial input with continuous dependence.
- **claim-moving-degree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-b-lem-moving-degree)): Let $I=[a,b]$, let $X$ be a real Banach space, and let $T:I\times X\to X$ be continuous and map bounded sets to relatively compact sets. Let $\mathcal U\subset I\times X$ be bounded and relatively open. Suppose no fixed point $Z=T(s,Z)$ belongs to the relative boundary of $\mathcal U$. Then, for $\mathcal U_s=\{Z:(s,Z)\in\mathcal U\}$, the Leray–Schauder degree $$\deg(I_X-T_s,\mathcal U_s,0)$$ is well defined and independent of $s$. Empty sections have degree zero. If $T_b$ is the zero map and $0\in\mathcal U_b$, the common degree is one, and every section contains a fixed point.
  - Explanation: Leray-Schauder degree is constant over varying open sets when no fixed point lies on the boundary.
- **claim-n3-existence-truncations** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-existence-deformation)): For the prepared domain of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">11</a> and every sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$, there is an integer $N_0\ge4$ and, for each $N\ge N_0$, a radius $R_{\min}(N)$, with $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$, such that the original deformation system has a smooth solution on every $\Omega_R$ with $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$. It satisfies $t>-\epsilon$ on the closure. At fixed $N$, these solutions have the local bounds of Proposition <a href="#n3:existence:classical-bounds" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:existence:classical-bounds">29</a>, uniformly as $R\to\infty$. In particular, any sequence $R_j\to\infty$ of such radii has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of $\overline\Omega$ to a solution of the original equations with $t\ge-\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: Smooth solutions with the floor excluded exist on every large truncation and have smooth local limits.
- **claim-n3-end-control** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-limit-end)): Fix $\epsilon>0$ and a sufficiently large $N\ge\max\{4,\lfloor2/\epsilon\rfloor+1\}$. The truncation solutions of Theorem <a href="#n3:existence:deformation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:existence:deformation">32</a> have a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of $\overline\Omega$ to a solution of the physical system with $t\ge-\epsilon$. On the asymptotically flat end, for some $c_N>0$ and fixed-$N$ constants $C_j(N)$, $$\|\nabla^j f\|\le C_j(N)e^{-c_N r} \quad\text{for each fixed }j,\qquad Z,t=O_2(r^{-1}).$$ The differences $t-Z$, $\bar g-g$, and their coordinate derivatives of any fixed order decay exponentially. The vector field $V$ satisfies $$\label{n3:limit:V-asymptote} V=4\nabla_g t+O(r^{-3})$$ and has a finite outward flux limit.
  - Explanation: The limiting solution decays exponentially in the graph and has controlled end asymptotics and finite flux.
- **claim-n3-geometry-adm** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-limit-geometry)): For the solution in Lemma <a href="#n3:limit:end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:limit:end">33</a>, $$\hat g=e^{4t}(g+l^2df^2)$$ is a smooth complete metric on $\overline\Omega$, with nonnegative scalar curvature and strictly negative mean curvature on $B$ for the normal pointing into $\Omega$. Its end is asymptotically flat with $$\hat g-\delta=O_2(r^{-1}),\qquad R_{\hat g}=O(r^{-3-\delta'}),\qquad \delta'=\min\{\delta,1\}>0,$$ where the reduced end has $R_g=O(r^{-3-\delta})$. If $$\mathfrak F_N=\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{S_r}V_\nu\,\mathrm dA_g,$$ then $$\label{n3:limit:adm} E_{\hat g}=E-\frac{\mathfrak F_N}{8\pi}.$$
  - Explanation: The deformed metric is complete with nonnegative scalar curvature, negative boundary mean curvature and an energy given by a flux formula.
- **claim-n3-flux-lower-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-limit-flux)): For fixed $\epsilon>0$, the physical solutions satisfy $$\mathfrak F_N\ge-\varepsilon_N,\qquad 0\le\varepsilon_N\le C(1+N)^C\bigl(\ell+\ell^2/\tau\bigr)\longrightarrow0.$$ All constants in this estimate are independent of the fixed-$N$ classical regularity constants.
  - Explanation: The flux is bounded below by a vanishing error with polynomial dependence.
- **claim-n3-reduced-energy** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-limit-energy)): The reduced data satisfy $$E\ge\sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.$$ Consequently Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">4</a> holds in its entire stated exterior class.
  - Explanation: The reduced data satisfy the energy-area inequality, which yields the exterior inequality in its whole class.
- **claim-four-weak-decay** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-b-four-weak)): Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary included, and with exactly one Euclidean coordinate end and compact complement. Assume $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad q>1.$$ Use the four-dimensional densities and ADM normalizations of Section [four:sec:output]. Suppose the densities are integrable, the finite ADM charges satisfy $E>\|P\|$, the dominant energy condition holds, and the boundary satisfies $H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{\mathrm{tan}}K\le0$ with normal into $M$. Then $$\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|^2}\ge \frac12\left(\frac{A_*(g)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}, \qquad \omega_3=2\pi^2,$$ where $A_*$ uses every full cut of Definition [four:def:cuts] [four:def:cuts](#four:def:cuts).
  - Explanation: For one-ended weakly decaying four-dimensional data the invariant mass is bounded below by the enclosing area power.
- **claim-maximal-end-equation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-b-transition-end)): Suppose $1<q<2$, $0<\delta<q-1$, $g-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$ on a four-dimensional end. Assume $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0$ and $R_g=O(r^{-4-\delta})$. For fixed $N,\varepsilon$, consider smooth solutions on successively larger spherical truncations, with $f=Z=0$ on the outer sphere, of <a href="#b:transition:trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="b:transition:trace">[b:transition:trace]</a> and $$\label{b:transition:divergence} \operatorname{div}_gV =u\left[\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+ \delta_0\eta_N \|w\|\|\nabla f\| -m_0(t)C_N(\rho_0+v\rho_1)\right].$$ Here $0<\delta_0<1$, $\rho,\rho_0=O(r^{-4-\delta})$ with their differentiated bounds, $\rho_1=O(r^{-2\gamma})$ for a fixed $\gamma>1$, $m_0$ is a smooth bounded function, and $\mathcal T$ is the quadratic term in the four-dimensional scalar identity. Assume that the solutions have a common bounded range and that, for every fixed derivative order, the background coefficients, weights and solutions have uniform fixed-$N$ classical bounds on end unit patches, including the outer boundary patches. Assume also that $A_\chi$ is uniformly elliptic there. These bounds may depend on $N$ and the derivative order; they are independent of the outer radius. They are separate assumptions from the displayed $O_2/O_1$ decay rates. Then, uniformly on those truncations, $$\|\nabla^j f\|\le C_j(N)e^{-c_j(N)r}\quad(j\ge0), \qquad \|Z\|+\|t\|\le C(N)r^{-2}.$$ Every smooth local limit satisfies $Z,t=O_2(r^{-2})$. Before taking that limit, its scalar equation is $$\label{b:transition:zero-graph} \begin{split} 3\Delta_g Z +3[p(Z)+2-\delta_0(p(Z)+1)]\|\,\mathrm dZ\|^2 ={}&\tfrac{\delta_0}{2}\|K\|^2+\rho -m_0(Z)C_N\rho_0+\mathcal E_N, \end{split}$$ where $\mathcal E_N$ and each required fixed derivative have exponential unit-patch bounds.
  - Explanation: Under maximality the graph decays exponentially and the conformal variable has quadratic decay with the tensor term retained.
- **claim-four-maximal-main** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-thm-main)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable initial-data exterior, diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^4$ minus an open ball, complete up to its connected compact boundary $S\cong S^3$, and with one asymptotically flat end. Here $K$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor. Assume the vacuum constraint equations with zero cosmological constant and maximality: $$\label{four:maximal:intro:constraints} R_g+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-\|K\|_g^2=0,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\bigl(K-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g\bigr)=0,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0.$$ Assume a smooth effective $T^2=U(1)\times U(1)$ action preserving $g,K$ which, in an asymptotically Euclidean chart $\mathbb R^4=\mathbb C^2$, is $$(e^{i\alpha},e^{i\beta})\cdot(z_1,z_2) =(e^{i\alpha}z_1,e^{i\beta}z_2)$$ at all sufficiently large radii. No cohomogeneity-one assumption is made. In that chart suppose $$\label{four:maximal:intro:decay} g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K_{ij}=O_1(r^{-q-1}),\qquad q>1.$$ Suppose the following ADM limits exist and are finite: $$\begin{aligned} E&=\frac{1}{6\omega_3}\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=r}(\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_ig_{jj}) \nu_\delta^i\,\mathrm dA_\delta,\label{four:maximal:intro:energy}\\ P_i&=\frac{1}{3\omega_3}\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=r}\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr) \nu_\delta^j\,\mathrm dA_\delta.\label{four:maximal:intro:momentum} \end{aligned}$$ Assume $P=0$ and $E>0$.* *Orient $S$ by its unit normal $\nu$ toward the end and set $H_S=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu$. Suppose $$\label{four:maximal:intro:mots} \Theta_K(S):=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=0.$$ Suppose $S$ is outermost toward the end: there is no compact smooth embedded two-sided hypersurface in the interior enclosing $S$, oriented toward the end, with $\Theta_K\le0$ everywhere. Suppose also that $S$ is outer area-minimizing: every compact smooth embedded enclosing hypersurface has three-volume at least $A=\|S\|_g$. Disconnected and noninvariant enclosing competitors are included. Then $$\label{four:maximal:intro:main-inequality} E\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A}{2\pi^2}\right)^{2/3}.$$
  - Explanation: For maximal vacuum four-dimensional exteriors with the stated symmetry and horizon hypotheses, energy is bounded below by the area power.
- **claim-four-maximal-output** (construction, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-geometric-output)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable four-dimensional ball exterior, complete including its compact boundary $S$, with one Euclidean coordinate end. Let $r\ge1$ be a fixed smooth positive extension of its Euclidean radius. Suppose $1<q<2$, $0<\delta<q-1$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0,\quad g-\delta_{\rm Eucl}=O_2(r^{-q}),\quad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\quad R_g=O(r^{-4-\delta}), \qquad \mu-\|J\|\ge c_0r^{-4-\delta}>0,$$ and suppose $H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK<0$. Assume finite ADM energy and uniform bounds of every fixed derivative order on end patches of unit size. Write $A_* =\mathcal A_g(S)$ for the infimum over all smooth enclosing cuts, including disconnected cuts.* *There is a smooth cut $B$ enclosing $S$, with connected one-ended exterior $\Omega$, such that for each $0<\epsilon<1$ and all sufficiently large integers $N$ there is a smooth metric $\widehat g_N$ on $\overline\Omega$ satisfying $$\widehat g_N\ge e^{-2\epsilon}g,\qquad R_{\widehat g_N}\ge0,\qquad \widehat H_B<0, \qquad E_{\widehat g_N}\le E_g+ \frac{\Pi_N}{3\omega_3} (e^{-\epsilon N}+e^{-\epsilon N/2}).$$ Here $\Pi_N$ has polynomial growth at fixed strict data and $\epsilon$. The new metric is complete including $B$, has $\widehat g_N-\delta_{\rm Eucl}=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $R_{\widehat g_N}=O(r^{-4-\delta})$, and every smooth cut enclosing $B$ has $\widehat g_N$-area at least $e^{-3\epsilon}A_*$.
  - Explanation: Strict maximal data admit deformed metrics with nonnegative scalar curvature, negative boundary mean curvature, an area lower bound and small energy error.
- **claim-four-maximal-strict-data** (construction, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-strict-data)): The data of Theorem <a href="#four:maximal:thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:maximal:thm:main">39</a> admit smooth approximations $(g_j,K_j)$ on the same exterior such that $$\begin{aligned} \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{g_j}K_j&=0,& \mu_j-\|J_j\|_{g_j}&\ge c_j r^{-4-\delta},\\ \Theta_{K_j}(S)&<0,& R_{g_j}&=O(r^{-4-\delta}), \qquad c_j>0. \end{aligned} \label{four:maximal:prep:strict-properties}$$ They have the prescribed $O_2(r^{-q})$ metric decay and $O_1(r^{-1-q})$ tensor decay, and all their coordinate derivatives are bounded uniformly over end patches of unit size, with constants allowed to depend on $j$ and the derivative order. Moreover, $$E_{g_j}\longrightarrow E_g, \qquad \mathcal A_{g_j}(S)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_g(S). \label{four:maximal:prep:approx-limits}$$ Consequently, it suffices to prove $E_g\ge\tfrac12(\mathcal A_g(S)/\omega_3)^{2/3}$ for such strict maximal data on this exterior. Neither vacuum nor marginality is required of the intermediate approximations.
  - Explanation: The original data are approximated by strict data with convergent energy and enclosing infimum.
- **claim-four-threshold-collars** (construction, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-threshold-collars)): There is a number $c$ with $\max_S\Theta_K<c<0$, and a closed filled compact region $\mathcal D_c$, containing a smooth compact filling of $S$ and an exterior collar of $S$, with the following properties. Its boundary $B$ is a smooth embedded stable threshold surface, $\Theta_K(B)=c$. It belongs to an increasing family $\mathcal D_b$, $\max_S\Theta_K<b<0$, of total regions at threshold $b$, all lying in a fixed compact set, and $$\mathcal D_{b}\longrightarrow\mathcal D_c \quad\text{in Hausdorff distance as }b\downarrow c. \label{four:maximal:prep:right-continuity}$$ The exterior $\Omega$ of $\mathcal D_c$ is connected and one-ended. Every smooth cut enclosing $B$ has $g$-area at least $A_*$. Each component of $B$ has a smooth outward collar with leaf coordinate $s\ge0$, $s=0$ at $B$, $\|\,\mathrm ds\|>0$, whose leaves satisfy $$\Theta_K(\{s=\text{constant}\})\ge c, \qquad \nu_s=\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}s}{\|\,\mathrm ds\|}. \label{four:maximal:prep:outward-collars}$$
  - Explanation: A right-continuous threshold region with outward collars and an area-preserving exterior exists.
- **claim-four-support-enclosure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-support-enclosure)): Let $A$ be a compact closed set containing $\mathcal D_c$. Suppose that every smooth exterior support to its frontier has expansion at most $k'$, where $c\le k'<0$. Then $$A\subset\mathcal D_{c'}\qquad\text{for every }k'<c'<0.$$ All expansions at the frontier of $A$ are computed in the original strict exterior data.
  - Explanation: A closed set with bounded exterior-support expansion lies inside a threshold region.
- **claim-four-scalar-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-scalar-identity)): For smooth $f,t$ satisfying <a href="#four:maximal:def:trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:maximal:def:trace">[four:maximal:def:trace]</a>, $$\label{four:maximal:def:scalar-identity} \frac12 e^{2t}R_{\widehat g} =\mu+J(w)+\mathcal T+w(F)-F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V,$$ where $$\begin{aligned} \label{four:maximal:def:quadratic-form} \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12\|T^0\|^2+\|M+(p+1)ay\|^2-v\|y\|^2 +3(p+1)(\|y\|^2+dx^2)\notag\\ &-\tfrac13(F-\chi j)^2+\chi j^2-\chi Fj+F^2 +2(p+1)\chi jax. \end{aligned}$$ This expression extends smoothly across $df=0$.
  - Explanation: The scalar identity of the four-dimensional warped graph metric.
- **claim-four-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-coercivity)): The quadratic form in <a href="#four:maximal:def:quadratic-form" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:maximal:def:quadratic-form">[four:maximal:def:quadratic-form]</a> is nonnegative, and $$\label{four:maximal:def:coercivity} \|T\|^2+\|M\|^2+dj^2+F^2+\|dt\|_{A_d}^2\le\Pi_N\mathcal T.$$ At $dt=0$ it has the stronger equivalence $$\label{four:maximal:def:coercivity-stationary} \mathcal T\asymp \|T^0\|^2+\|M\|^2+\chi j^2+F^2,$$ with both constants absolute, independent of $N,d,\chi$.
  - Explanation: The four-dimensional quadratic form is nonnegative and pointwise controls the deformation variables.
- **claim-four-boundary-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-boundary-identity)): On a hypersurface where $f$ is constant, let $H$ denote its $g$-mean curvature for a chosen normal $\nu$, and put $P_B=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_BK$. Then $$\begin{aligned} V_\nu/u&=d(H+3\partial_\nu t)-H+w_\nu(F-P_B), \label{four:maximal:def:boundary-flux}\\ \widehat H&=e^{-t}\sqrt d\,(H+3\partial_\nu t). \label{four:maximal:def:boundary-curvature} \end{aligned}$$ The identities allow either sign of $\partial_\nu f$, including zero.
  - Explanation: Boundary flux and mean curvature identities hold on constant-height hypersurfaces.
- **claim-four-height-end** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-height-end)): Every smooth homotopy solution satisfies $\|h\|+\|F\|\le C_0$ for a fixed constant independent of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameter. There are fixed $r_0,C_2$ such that, for all sufficiently large $R$ depending on $N,\epsilon$, the first three stages satisfy $$\label{four:maximal:def:height-end} \|h\|\le C_2(r^{-\gamma}-R^{-\gamma})\quad(r_0\le r\le R), \qquad \|\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}f\|\big\|_{S_R}\le C_3\eta_N^{-1}R^{-1-\gamma}.$$ Moreover $t>-\epsilon$ on $S_R$. None of these assertions assumes an interior lower bound for $t$.
  - Explanation: Height and trace right side are bounded uniformly in the homotopy.
- **claim-four-gauss-minimum** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-def-gauss-minimum)): At an interior minimum of $t$, $$\label{four:maximal:def:graph-gauss} \tfrac12e^{2t}R_{\widehat g} \le\tfrac12R_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e_f,e_f)+\mathcal S(H^f),$$ where, for a symmetric tensor $A$, $$\label{four:maximal:def:gauss-form} \mathcal S(A)=\tfrac13(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A)^2 -\tfrac12\|A_\perp^0\|^2 +dA_{ee}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A-d\|A_{e\perp}\|^2.$$ At every point where $dt=0$, there is an absolute $c_2>0$ such that $$\label{four:maximal:def:floor-comparison} \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f) \ge c_2\mathcal T-\Pi_N\bigl(vF^2+\|K\|^2\bigr).$$ At $df=0$ the terms multiplied by $v$ vanish and any axis may be used.
  - Explanation: At an interior minimum of the conformal variable the scalar curvature is compared with a Gauss form.
- **claim-four-coefficient-derivatives** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-def-coefficient-lemma)): The following estimates hold along every smooth trace solution: $$\label{four:maximal:def:derivative-bounds} \|\nabla w\|+\|\nabla A_\chi\|+\|d\log u\|_{A_\chi} \le\Pi_N(\sqrt{\mathcal T}+\|K\|).$$ Consequently, for each fixed $\eta_1>0$, $$\label{four:maximal:def:drift-divergence} \frac{\|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uA_\chi K(w,\cdot))\|}{u} \le\eta_1\mathcal T+\Pi_N\bigl(\|K\|^2+a\|\nabla K\|\bigr).$$ In each of the first three trace stages, $$\label{four:maximal:def:F-derivative} w(F)\ge\eta_N a\sigma-\eta_1\mathcal T -\Pi_N\bigl(\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+\|K\|^2+a\|\nabla K\|\bigr),$$ where $\mathcal K$ is a fixed compact enlargement of the supports of $C,D_0,D_1$. For fixed $\eta_1$ the bounds remain polynomial in $N$.
  - Explanation: Derivatives of the coefficients are controlled with polynomial constants along trace solutions.
- **claim-four-floor-exclusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-floor)): There is a choice $0<\delta_0<1/4$ independent of $N$ and a positive polynomial $C_N$ such that, for every sufficiently large allowed $R$, no smooth solution of any of the four homotopy stages has $$\min_{\overline{\Omega_R}}t=-\epsilon.$$ These choices use the fixed data and the preceding pointwise and height estimates only. In particular they do not use existence, an upper bound for $Z$, or a uniform Hessian estimate.
  - Explanation: No solution of any homotopy stage reaches the conformal floor.
- **claim-four-separation** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-separation)): Let $Q_0$ be a compact subset of $\overline\Omega$ disjoint from $\mathcal D_c$. There are $\eta_2>0$, $N_0$, and allowed radii $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$ such that, in stages 1 and 2, $$\label{four:maximal:bounds:separation} h\ge c+\eta_2\quad\hbox{on }Q_0 \qquad(N\ge N_0,\ R\ge R_{\min}(N)).$$ The constants are uniform over both stages.
  - Explanation: The height is uniformly separated from the threshold on compact sets away from the threshold region in the first two stages.
- **claim-four-collar-slopes** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-collar-slopes)): For all sufficiently large $N$ and allowed $R$, there are fixed constants $0<c_5<C_6$ such that $$\label{four:maximal:bounds:collar-slopes} \frac{c_5}{\eta_N}\le\partial_\nu f\le\frac{C_6}{\eta_N} \quad\hbox{in stages 1 and 2},\qquad \|\partial_\nu f\|\le\frac{C_6}{\eta_N} \quad\hbox{in stage 3}.$$ Here $\nu$ points into $\Omega$. In stage 4, $f=0$.
  - Explanation: Inner collar slopes are bounded above and below by fixed multiples of the inverse parameter.
- **claim-four-weighted-trace** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-weighted-trace)): Let $\mathcal C$ be a fixed union of collars. In stages 1 and 2, every nonnegative $C^1$ function $\varphi$ satisfies $$\begin{aligned} \int_B L_0\varphi &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C} u\bigl((1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi+\|\,\mathrm d\varphi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr), \label{four:maximal:bounds:trace-weighted}\\ \int_B\varphi &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C} \sqrt D\bigl((1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi+\|\,\mathrm d\varphi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr). \label{four:maximal:bounds:trace-unweighted} \end{aligned}$$ The integrands vanish outside the support of $\varphi$ and its derivative; thus both statements localize to any base patch. Moreover $$\label{four:maximal:bounds:boundary-flux} \|(V_\lambda)_\nu\|\le C_7ud=C_7L_0\sqrt d \le C_8(\eta_N/\ell)L_0.$$ Consequently, $$\label{four:maximal:bounds:boundary-absorption} \int_B\|(V_\lambda)_\nu\| \le \Pi_N\frac{\eta_N}{\ell} \int_{\mathcal C}u(\rho+\delta_0\mathcal T).$$ All constants in these assertions have the stated polynomial control.
  - Explanation: Weighted and unweighted boundary traces and the boundary flux are bounded polynomially.
- **claim-four-bounded-range** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-bounded-range)): For every sufficiently large fixed $N$ and all sufficiently large allowed $R$, every admissible smooth homotopy solution satisfies $$\label{four:maximal:bounds:bounded-range} \|f\|\le C_0/\eta_N,\qquad -\epsilon\le t\le Z\le C(N),\qquad \|\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}f\|\le C(N).$$ The constants are independent of $R$, the solution, and the homotopy parameter. No uniform Hessian or coefficient continuity estimate is used in obtaining these bounds.
  - Explanation: Height, conformal variable and gradient are bounded for admissible solutions.
- **claim-four-classical-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-classical-estimates)): Fix the strict data, $\epsilon$, a sufficiently large $N$, and any of the homotopy stages of Section <a href="#four:maximal:sec:deformation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:maximal:sec:deformation">12</a>. Every smooth solution on an allowed finite truncation with $t\ge-\epsilon$ has uniform local bounds for every finite number of derivatives of $f$ and $Z$, including up to the inner and outer boundary faces. On the uniform unit patches on the end these constants are independent of the outer truncation radius and of the stage parameter. They may depend arbitrarily on $N$. In particular, on a fixed finite truncation they bound the $C^{1,\alpha}$ norm of $Z$ for each fixed $0<\alpha<1$.
  - Explanation: Uniform local bounds of every finite order hold up to both boundary faces.
- **claim-four-scalar-solve** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-scalar-solve)): For every $Z\in C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega_R)$ and every homotopy parameter $s$, the trace equation with its assigned constant Dirichlet values has a unique solution $f=f_s[Z]\in C^{3,\alpha}(\overline\Omega_R)$. No lower bound on $t=t(Z,\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}f)$ is assumed. On bounded sets of trial inputs, these solutions have bounded $C^{3,\alpha}$ norms, uniformly in $s$. The map $(s,Z)\mapsto f_s[Z]$ is continuous into $C^{3,\alpha}$ and is locally obtained by inversion of the scalar Dirichlet operator.
  - Explanation: The trace equation has a unique regular solution for every trial input.
- **claim-four-existence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-existence)): For the fixed strict data and every $0<\epsilon<1$ there are $N_0$ and $R_{\min}(N)$, with $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$, such that for every integer $N\ge N_0$ and every $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$ the desired coupled system has a smooth solution on $\overline\Omega_R$ with $t>-\epsilon$. At each such fixed $N$, a subsequence as $R\to\infty$ converges smoothly on compact subsets of $\overline\Omega$ to a solution of the equations and inner boundary conditions with $t\ge-\epsilon$. The previously proved height, range and collar estimates hold for this limit.
  - Explanation: Solutions exist on large truncations and subconverge as the radius grows.
- **claim-four-end-control** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-end-control)): The exhaustion solutions of Proposition <a href="#four:maximal:prop:existence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:maximal:prop:existence">58</a> admit a smooth local limit $(f,Z)$ on $\overline\Omega$ satisfying the desired system and $t\ge-\epsilon$. Every such limit has $$\label{four:maximal:end:decay} \|\nabla^j f\|\le C_j(N)e^{-c_j(N)r}\quad(j\ge0), \qquad Z,t=O_2(r^{-2}).$$ The zeroth-order estimates producing this normalization are uniform on the finite truncations. The resulting metric $\widehat g=e^{2t}(g+l^2df\otimes df)$ is smooth, complete with its boundary included, and asymptotically flat with $$\label{four:maximal:end:geometry} \widehat g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad 0\le R_{\widehat g}=O(r^{-4-\delta}),\qquad \widehat H_B<0.$$ Here the normal defining $\widehat H_B$ points toward infinity.
  - Explanation: The limit has exponentially decaying graph, quadratic conformal decay and a complete asymptotically flat metric with the geometric signs.
- **claim-four-flux-mass** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-prop-flux)): For the limiting solution at fixed $N$, the flux $$\mathfrak F=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}V\cdot\nu_g\,\mathrm dA_g$$ exists and satisfies $$\label{four:maximal:end:mass-flux} E_{\widehat g}=E_g-\frac{\mathfrak F}{3\omega_3}, \qquad \omega_3=2\pi^2.$$ There is a polynomial bound $\Pi_N$, independent of the exhaustion radius and of the fixed-$N$ regularity constants, such that $$\label{four:maximal:end:flux-deficit} \mathfrak F\ge-\Pi_N\left(\ell+\frac{\ell^2}{\eta_N}\right).$$ Consequently, for fixed strict data and $\epsilon>0$, $E_{\widehat g}\le E_g+o(1)$ as $N\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: The flux exists, determines the energy change, and has a lower bound that vanishes against polynomial losses.
- **claim-four-minimal-enclosure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-maximal-lem-minimal-enclosure)): The metric $\widehat g$ of Proposition <a href="#four:maximal:prop:end-control" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:maximal:prop:end-control">59</a> admits a nonempty compact smooth embedded minimal hypersurface $\Sigma$ enclosing $B$. Its exterior is connected, complete with boundary, and has the same single asymptotically flat end. The hypersurface is outer area-minimizing, with disconnected competitors permitted, and its area $\widehat A=\|\Sigma\|_{\widehat g}$ satisfies $$\label{four:maximal:end:area-comparison} \widehat A\ge e^{-3\epsilon}A_*.$$
  - Explanation: The deformed metric has an outer area-minimizing minimal enclosure with an area lower bound.

```json
        "anchor": "stmt-n3-domains-stable-collar",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(N^d,g)$ be smooth, with $d\\in\\{3,4\\}$ and a fixed smooth symmetric tensor $Q$. Let $\\Sigma$ be a compact connected smooth two-sided hypersurface without boundary, forming a component of the frontier of a closed region $D$, with normal pointing out of $D$. Assume $\\Theta_Q(\\Sigma)=c$ and stability for outward variations. Assume also local *outward-replacement maximality*: in some collar of $\\Sigma$ disjoint from the other frontier components and all designated barrier faces, no positive outward normal graph can replace $\\Sigma$, leaving $D$ unchanged outside that collar, and have expansion at most $c$ everywhere on the new component. There is a smooth foliation $\\Sigma_s$, $0\\leq s<s_0$, of an outward collar, with $\\Sigma_0=\\Sigma$ and positive outward normal velocity, such that $$\\label{n3:domains:collar-expansion}\n \\Theta_Q(\\Sigma_s)>c\\quad(0<s<s_0),\\qquad\n \\Theta_Q(\\Sigma_0)=c.$$ In particular its leaf parameter $s$ is a smooth defining function and $|\\nabla s|$ is bounded above and below by positive constants.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $(N^d,g,Q)$ be smooth, with $d\\in\\{3,4\\}$.         "anchor": "stmt-n3-domains-weak-support",
        "exact_quote": "Let $N$ be a smooth compact connected three-manifold with boundary $\\Gamma_-\\sqcup\\Gamma_+$, where $\\Gamma_+$ is nonempty and $\\Gamma_-$ may be empty. Let $D$ be a nonempty closed subset which contains a relative collar of $\\Gamma_-$ when that boundary is prescribed, and stays a positive distance from $\\Gamma_+$. Suppose its interior frontier has exterior-support expansion at most $c$ for a smooth tensor $Q$.*\n\n\n*For every $c'>c$ such that $\\Theta_Q(\\Gamma_+)>c'$ with its normal out of $N$, there is a smooth bounding domain $E$ containing $D$ in its relative interior, containing the required inner collar, and avoiding $\\Gamma_+$, whose free boundary satisfies $$\\label{n3:domains:smooth-enclosure-expansion}\n \\Theta_Q(\\partial E\\setminus\\Gamma_-)=c'.$$ Its boundary and the domain may be disconnected.         "anchor": "stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain",
        "exact_quote": "The thresholds and the domain above can be chosen with the following properties. The numbers $c_b,c_w<0$ are right-continuity points of their respective full maximal-region families. The boundary of $\\Omega$ consists of the faces in Equation <a href=\"#n3:domains:face-expansions\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:domains:face-expansions\">[n3:domains:face-expansions]</a>, has disjoint smooth outward leaf collars as in Lemma <a href=\"#n3:domains:stable-collar\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:domains:stable-collar\">7</a>, and preserves the enclosing-area lower bound in Equation <a href=\"#n3:domains:inherited-area\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:domains:inherited-area\">[n3:domains:inherited-area]</a>.*\n\n\n*There are a smooth compactly supported function $C$ on $\\Omega$, constants $C_b\\geq0$, $C_w\\leq0$, and positive constants $k_B$ on its face collars such that $$\\label{n3:domains:offset-collars}\n \\begin{aligned}\n  C_w\\leq C\\leq C_b,&\\qquad\n  C=C_b-k_Bs&&\\text{in a black collar near }B_b,\\\\\n  &\\qquad C=C_w+k_Bs&&\\text{in a white collar near }B_w.\n \\end{aligned}$$ For an absent type, its corresponding constant is simply a bound. Set $$\\label{n3:domains:assigned-heights}\n b_-=c_b-C_b<0,\n \\qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0.$$ There is a smooth positive function $\\rho$, equal to a positive constant times $r^{-4}$ on the far end and satisfying symbol derivative bounds there, such that, for every $h\\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$\\label{n3:domains:offset-smallness}\n |(h+C)\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}K|+|\\nabla C|+\\rho\n      \\leq\\tfrac12\\mathfrak m\n \\quad\\hbox{everywhere on }\\Omega.$$ The thresholds, collars, offset, and $\\rho$ are fixed before the deformation parameters are chosen. After fixing the thresholds and collars, the offset and its first derivatives can be made arbitrarily small.",

        "anchor": "stmt-n3-deformation-identity",
        "exact_quote": "Let $f,t$ be smooth and $F=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\\chi}(K+H^f)$. At $\\sigma>0$ decompose $S$ relative to $\\mathbb Re\\oplus e^\\perp$: $$T=S|_{e^\\perp\\times e^\\perp},\\quad\n M=S(e,\\cdot)|_{e^\\perp},\\quad q=S(e,e),\\quad \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}T=F-\\chi q.$$ Then $$\\label{n3:deformation:scalar-identity}\n \\begin{split}\n \\tfrac12e^{4t}\\mathop{\\mathrm{Scal}}_{\\hat g}\n ={}&8\\pi(\\mu+J(w))+\\mathcal T\n       +w(F)-F\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}V,\n \\end{split}$$ where $$\\label{n3:deformation:quadratic-term}\n \\begin{split}\n \\mathcal T={}&\\tfrac12|T^{\\operatorname{tf}}|^2\n +(M+pa\\nabla_\\perp t)\\cdot(M+(p+2)a\\nabla_\\perp t)\\\\\n &+4(p+1)|\\,\\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2\n   +(\\chi-\\chi^2/4)q^2+2(p+1)\\chi qa\\,\\partial_e t\\\\\n &-\\chi Fq/2+3F^2/4.\n \\end{split}$$ After substituting $F=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\\chi}S$, this expression extends smoothly across $\\sigma=0$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.12"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-n3-deformation-identity",

        "anchor": "stmt-n3-apriori-sublevel-support",
        "exact_quote": "Let $U$ be an open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $d\\in\\{3,4\\}$, let $Q$ be a smooth symmetric tensor on $U$, and let $u:U\\to\\mathbb R$ be finite and lower semicontinuous. Fix $k<k'$ and $q_0\\in\\mathbb R$. A smooth lower test of $u$ at $x$ is a smooth function $\\phi$ with $\\phi(x)=u(x)$ and $\\phi\\le u$ near $x$. Suppose every such test with $u(x)<k'$ and $\\,\\mathrm d\\phi(x)\\ne0$ satisfies $$\\mathcal E_Q[\\phi](x)\\le q_0,$$ where $\\mathcal E_Q$ is the expansion in Equation <a href=\"#n3:domains:test-expansion\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:domains:test-expansion\">[n3:domains:test-expansion]</a> of the regular level through $x$, oriented toward increasing $\\phi$. Equivalently, subtract $\\phi(x)$ before applying that formula.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n3-existence-gradient",
        "exact_quote": "Let $U'$ be compactly contained in an interior or boundary coordinate patch $U$ in dimension three. In a boundary patch assume that $z$ is constant on the boundary face. Suppose $z$ is $C^3$, up to that face when present, $|\\nabla z|\\le L$, and, almost everywhere, $$\\label{n3:existence:axial-equation}\n A_\\chi:\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}z=G,\\qquad\n A_\\chi=I-(1-\\chi)e\\otimes e,\\qquad\n e=\\frac{\\nabla z}{|\\nabla z|},\\qquad\n 0<\\chi_0\\le\\chi\\le1,$$ where $\\|G\\|_\\infty\\le Q$. At zero gradients any measurable unit axis for which the equation holds is allowed. Then there are $\\alpha\\in(0,1)$ and $C<\\infty$, depending only on $\\chi_0$, the patch geometry and the separation of $U'$ from the other patch boundaries, such that $$\\label{n3:existence:gradient-estimate}\n \\|\\nabla z\\|_{C^{0,\\alpha}(U')}\n \\le C(L+Q).$$ For all sufficiently small coordinate balls centered in $U'$, with intersection with the domain understood at a boundary, one also has $$\\label{n3:existence:hessian-morrey}\n \\int_{B_r\\cap U}|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}z|^2\\,\\mathrm dV_g\n \\le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\\alpha}.$$ In particular, the constants are independent of continuity moduli of $\\chi$ and $G$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.12"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-n3-existence-gradient",
          "exact_quote": "Let $U'$ be compactly contained in an interior or boundary coordinate patch $U$ in dimension three. In a boundary patch assume that $z$ is constant on the boundary face. Suppose $z$ is $C^3$, up to that face when present, $|\\nabla z|\\le L$, and, almost everywhere, $$\\label{n3:existence:axial-equation}\n A_\\chi:\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}z=G,\\qquad\n A_\\chi=I-(1-\\chi)e\\otimes e,\\qquad\n e=\\frac{\\nabla z}{|\\nabla z|},\\qquad\n 0<\\chi_0\\le\\chi\\le1,$$ where $\\|G\\|_\\infty\\le Q$. At zero gradients any measurable unit axis for which the equation holds is allowed. Then there are $\\alpha\\in(0,1)$ and $C<\\infty$, depending only on $\\chi_0$, the patch geometry and the separation of $U'$ from the other patch boundaries, such that $$\\label{n3:existence:gradient-estimate}\n \\|\\nabla z\\|_{C^{0,\\alpha}(U')}\n \\le C(L+Q).$$ For all sufficiently small coordinate balls centered in $U'$, with intersection with the domain understood at a boundary, one also has $$\\label{n3:existence:hessian-morrey}\n \\int_{B_r\\cap U}|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}z|^2\\,\\mathrm dV_g\n \\le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\\alpha}.$$ In particular, the constants are independent of continuity moduli of $\\chi$ and $G$.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.12"
        }

        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"n3:existence:natural-growth\" label=\"n3:existence:natural-growth\"></span>Let $n\\in\\{3,4\\}$ and let $Z\\in L^\\infty\\cap W^{1,2}_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ on a ball in $\\mathbb R^n$. Fix a Borel representative with $|Z|\\le M$ for products with measures. Suppose, in distributions, that $$\\label{n3:existence:natural-equation}\n \\operatorname{div}(aDZ+b)=e,$$ where $a$ is measurable and symmetric, $\\lambda I\\le a\\le\\Lambda I$ for $0<\\lambda\\le\\Lambda$, $|b|\\le B$, and $e$ is a signed measure satisfying $$\\label{n3:existence:natural-source}\n |e|\\le C_0(1+|DZ|^2)\\,\\mathrm dx+\\mu,\\qquad\n \\mu(B_r(x))\\le C_\\mu r^{n-2+\\beta},\\qquad \\beta>0.$$ Here $\\mu$ is a positive measure, and its bound holds at every center and all sufficiently small radii in a larger patch. Assume the weak exponential product rule <a href=\"#n3:existence:exponential-identity\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:existence:exponential-identity\">[n3:existence:exponential-identity]</a> below is valid with the specified representative. This is true, in particular, for a function continuous across a flat interface and smooth on its two closed sides, when the equation includes the normal-flux jump. Then the Sobolev class of $Z$ has a Hölder representative on smaller balls, with constants depending only on the displayed bounds and patch separation. If $Z$ is already continuous, this is a uniform estimate for that function. The conclusion applies up to a smooth face whenever its reflected equation satisfies these hypotheses.",

        "anchor": "stmt-n3-existence-scalar-solve",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $N\\ge4$, $\\tau>0$, a finite smooth truncation $\\Omega_R$, and a homotopy parameter $s\\in[0,4]$. For every $Z\\in C^{1,b}(\\overline{\\Omega_R})$, $0<b<1$, the scalar trace equation of Proposition <a href=\"#n3:deformation:homotopy\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:deformation:homotopy\">15</a>, with its prescribed componentwise constant Dirichlet values for $f$, has a unique solution. It lies in $C^{3,b}$ and is smooth to the extent allowed by the input. The solution operator $$\\label{n3:existence:scalar-operator}\n f=\\mathcal S_s(Z)$$ is continuous in $(s,Z)$, including across the concatenation points of the homotopy. On bounded subsets of $C^{1,b}$ its $C^{3,b}$ norm is uniformly bounded at these fixed parameters. No lower bound for $t$ is required.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-b-lem-moving-degree",
        "exact_quote": "Let $I=[a,b]$, let $X$ be a real Banach space, and let $T:I\\times X\\to X$ be continuous and map bounded sets to relatively compact sets. Let $\\mathcal U\\subset I\\times X$ be bounded and relatively open. Suppose no fixed point $Z=T(s,Z)$ belongs to the relative boundary of $\\mathcal U$. Then, for $\\mathcal U_s=\\{Z:(s,Z)\\in\\mathcal U\\}$, the Leray–Schauder degree $$\\deg(I_X-T_s,\\mathcal U_s,0)$$ is well defined and independent of $s$. Empty sections have degree zero. If $T_b$ is the zero map and $0\\in\\mathcal U_b$, the common degree is one, and every section contains a fixed point.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.12"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-n3-existence-deformation",
        "exact_quote": "For the prepared domain of Proposition <a href=\"#n3:domains:prepared-domain\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:domains:prepared-domain\">11</a> and every sufficiently small fixed $\\epsilon>0$, there is an integer $N_0\\ge4$ and, for each $N\\ge N_0$, a radius $R_{\\min}(N)$, with $R_{\\min}(N)\\to\\infty$, such that the original deformation system has a smooth solution on every $\\Omega_R$ with $R\\ge R_{\\min}(N)$. It satisfies $t>-\\epsilon$ on the closure. At fixed $N$, these solutions have the local bounds of Proposition <a href=\"#n3:existence:classical-bounds\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:existence:classical-bounds\">29</a>, uniformly as $R\\to\\infty$.         "exact_quote": "For the solution in Lemma <a href=\"#n3:limit:end\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:limit:end\">33</a>, $$\\hat g=e^{4t}(g+l^2df^2)$$ is a smooth complete metric on $\\overline\\Omega$, with nonnegative scalar curvature and strictly negative mean curvature on $B$ for the normal pointing into $\\Omega$.         "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary included, and with exactly one Euclidean coordinate end and compact complement. Suppose the densities are integrable, the finite ADM charges satisfy $E>|P|$, the dominant energy condition holds, and the boundary satisfies $H+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{\\mathrm{tan}}K\\le0$ with normal into $M$.         "exact_quote": "Suppose $1<q<2$, $0<\\delta<q-1$, $g-\\delta_{\\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$ on a four-dimensional end. Assume $\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0$ and $R_g=O(r^{-4-\\delta})$. For fixed $N,\\varepsilon$, consider smooth solutions on successively larger spherical truncations, with $f=Z=0$ on the outer sphere, of <a href=\"#b:transition:trace\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"b:transition:trace\">[b:transition:trace]</a> and $$\\label{b:transition:divergence}\n \\operatorname{div}_gV\n =u\\left[\\delta_0\\mathcal T+\\rho+\n       \\delta_0\\eta_N |w||\\nabla f|\n       -m_0(t)C_N(\\rho_0+v\\rho_1)\\right].$$ Here $0<\\delta_0<1$, $\\rho,\\rho_0=O(r^{-4-\\delta})$ with their differentiated bounds, $\\rho_1=O(r^{-2\\gamma})$ for a fixed $\\gamma>1$, $m_0$ is a smooth bounded function, and $\\mathcal T$ is the quadratic term in the four-dimensional scalar identity. Assume that the solutions have a common bounded range and that, for every fixed derivative order, the background coefficients, weights and solutions have uniform fixed-$N$ classical bounds on end unit patches, including the outer boundary patches. Assume also that $A_\\chi$ is uniformly elliptic there. These bounds may depend on $N$ and the derivative order; they are independent of the outer radius. They are separate assumptions from the displayed $O_2/O_1$ decay rates. Then, uniformly on those truncations, $$|\\nabla^j f|\\le C_j(N)e^{-c_j(N)r}\\quad(j\\ge0),\n \\qquad |Z|+|t|\\le C(N)r^{-2}.$$ Every smooth local limit satisfies $Z,t=O_2(r^{-2})$. Before taking that limit, its scalar equation is $$\\label{b:transition:zero-graph}\n \\begin{split}\n 3\\Delta_g Z\n +3[p(Z)+2-\\delta_0(p(Z)+1)]|\\,\\mathrm dZ|^2\n ={}&\\tfrac{\\delta_0}{2}|K|^2+\\rho\n       -m_0(Z)C_N\\rho_0+\\mathcal E_N,\n \\end{split}$$ where $\\mathcal E_N$ and each required fixed derivative have exponential unit-patch bounds.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-four-maximal-thm-main",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable initial-data exterior, diffeomorphic to $\\mathbb R^4$ minus an open ball, complete up to its connected compact boundary $S\\cong S^3$, and with one asymptotically flat end. Here $K$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor. Assume the vacuum constraint equations with zero cosmological constant and maximality: $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:constraints}\n R_g+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-|K|_g^2=0,\\qquad\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\bigl(K-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g\\bigr)=0,\\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0.$$ Assume a smooth effective $T^2=U(1)\\times U(1)$ action preserving $g,K$ which, in an asymptotically Euclidean chart $\\mathbb R^4=\\mathbb C^2$, is $$(e^{i\\alpha},e^{i\\beta})\\cdot(z_1,z_2)\n       =(e^{i\\alpha}z_1,e^{i\\beta}z_2)$$ at all sufficiently large radii. No cohomogeneity-one assumption is made. In that chart suppose $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:decay}\n g_{ij}-\\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad\n K_{ij}=O_1(r^{-q-1}),\\qquad q>1.$$ Suppose the following ADM limits exist and are finite: $$\\begin{aligned}\n E&=\\frac{1}{6\\omega_3}\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n     \\int_{|x|=r}(\\partial_jg_{ij}-\\partial_ig_{jj})\n                  \\nu_\\delta^i\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta,\\label{four:maximal:intro:energy}\\\\\n P_i&=\\frac{1}{3\\omega_3}\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n     \\int_{|x|=r}\\bigl(K_{ij}-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\\bigr)\n                  \\nu_\\delta^j\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta.\\label{four:maximal:intro:momentum}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Assume $P=0$ and $E>0$.*\n\n\n*Orient $S$ by its unit normal $\\nu$ toward the end and set $H_S=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_S\\nu$. Suppose $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:mots}\n \\Theta_K(S):=H_S+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_SK=0.$$ Suppose $S$ is outermost toward the end: there is no compact smooth embedded two-sided hypersurface in the interior enclosing $S$, oriented toward the end, with $\\Theta_K\\le0$ everywhere. Suppose also that $S$ is outer area-minimizing: every compact smooth embedded enclosing hypersurface has three-volume at least $A=|S|_g$. Disconnected and noninvariant enclosing competitors are included. Then $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:main-inequality}\n E\\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A}{2\\pi^2}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.12"
      },

No cohomogeneity-one assumption is made. In that chart suppose $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:decay}\n g_{ij}-\\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad\n K_{ij}=O_1(r^{-q-1}),\\qquad q>1.$$ Suppose the following ADM limits exist and are finite: $$\\begin{aligned}\n E&=\\frac{1}{6\\omega_3}\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n     \\int_{|x|=r}(\\partial_jg_{ij}-\\partial_ig_{jj})\n                  \\nu_\\delta^i\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta,\\label{four:maximal:intro:energy}\\\\\n P_i&=\\frac{1}{3\\omega_3}\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n     \\int_{|x|=r}\\bigl(K_{ij}-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\\bigr)\n                  \\nu_\\delta^j\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta.\\label{four:maximal:intro:momentum}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Assume $P=0$ and $E>0$.*\n\n\n*Orient $S$ by its unit normal $\\nu$ toward the end and set $H_S=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_S\\nu$. Suppose $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:mots}\n \\Theta_K(S):=H_S+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_SK=0.$$ Suppose $S$ is outermost toward the end: there is no compact smooth embedded two-sided hypersurface in the interior enclosing $S$, oriented toward the end, with $\\Theta_K\\le0$ everywhere. Suppose also that $S$ is outer area-minimizing: every compact smooth embedded enclosing hypersurface has three-volume at least $A=|S|_g$. Disconnected and noninvariant enclosing competitors are included. Then $$\\label{four:maximal:intro:main-inequality}\n E\\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A}{2\\pi^2}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",

        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable four-dimensional ball exterior, complete including its compact boundary $S$, with one Euclidean coordinate end.         "exact_quote": "There is a number $c$ with $\\max_S\\Theta_K<c<0$, and a closed filled compact region $\\mathcal D_c$, containing a smooth compact filling of $S$ and an exterior collar of $S$, with the following properties.         "exact_quote": "For smooth $f,t$ satisfying <a href=\"#four:maximal:def:trace\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"four:maximal:def:trace\">[four:maximal:def:trace]</a>, $$\\label{four:maximal:def:scalar-identity}\n \\frac12 e^{2t}R_{\\widehat g}\n =\\mu+J(w)+\\mathcal T+w(F)-F\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}V,$$ where $$\\begin{aligned}\n\\label{four:maximal:def:quadratic-form}\n \\mathcal T={}&\\tfrac12|T^0|^2+|M+(p+1)ay|^2-v|y|^2\n       +3(p+1)(|y|^2+dx^2)\\notag\\\\\n &-\\tfrac13(F-\\chi j)^2+\\chi j^2-\\chi Fj+F^2\n       +2(p+1)\\chi jax.\n\\end{aligned}$$ This expression extends smoothly across $df=0$.",

        "exact_quote": "The quadratic form in <a href=\"#four:maximal:def:quadratic-form\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"four:maximal:def:quadratic-form\">[four:maximal:def:quadratic-form]</a> is nonnegative, and $$\\label{four:maximal:def:coercivity}\n |T|^2+|M|^2+dj^2+F^2+|dt|_{A_d}^2\\le\\Pi_N\\mathcal T.$$ At $dt=0$ it has the stronger equivalence $$\\label{four:maximal:def:coercivity-stationary}\n \\mathcal T\\asymp |T^0|^2+|M|^2+\\chi j^2+F^2,$$ with both constants absolute, independent of $N,d,\\chi$.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a fixed union of collars. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
```
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Exterior and enclosing cut** ([source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-class)): An exterior is a connected orientable smooth three-manifold $\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary, complete as a metric space with its boundary included, and with one asymptotically flat coordinate end whose complement is compact. An enclosing cut is the entire compact smooth embedded two-sided intrinsic boundary of a connected smooth end-containing domain $D$ closed in $\overline\Omega$, whose intrinsic interior lies in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$. It separates the entire inner boundary from the distant end. The inner side includes the original obstacle and every bounded complementary pocket. All components of the cut and every portion coincident with the inner boundary are counted. Its normal points into $D$, toward the end. We put $$a_g(\partial\Omega)= \inf\{\|\Gamma\|_g:\Gamma\text{ is an enclosing cut}\}.$$ When using perimeter compactness, we take the closure of this class among filled inner sets and include the area of any frontier coinciding with the obstacle. Smooth outward approximation gives the same infimum. Enclosing cuts and minimizing sets are taken with bounded complementary pockets filled. Auxiliary perimeter arguments may use competitors containing the inner obstacle before filling: filling a bounded pocket deletes its frontier, cannot increase perimeter, and leaves the enclosing infimum unchanged.
- **Prepared three-dimensional data** ([source](#stmt-n3-prepared-data)): Let $(\Omega_0,g,K)$ be an exterior in Definition <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-class">1</a>, with inner boundary $S_0$. Suppose $K$ is compactly supported and, on its single coordinate end, $g-\delta=O_j(r^{-1})$ for every fixed $j\ge0$. Assume the physical constraint densities in Equation <a href="#n3:intro:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:constraints">[n3:intro:constraints]</a> are integrable, the ADM energy is $E>0$, and the ADM momentum is zero. There are $0<\delta<1$, $c>0$, and a smooth radius extension $\varrho\ge1$, equal to $r$ sufficiently far out, such that $$R_g=O(r^{-3-\delta}),\qquad 8\pi(\mu-\|J\|_g)\ge c\varrho^{-3-\delta}.$$ The boundary is strictly future trapped with its normal into the exterior: $\theta_+(S_0)<0$ on every component. Its full enclosing-area infimum is denoted by $A_*=a_g(S_0)>0$.
- **Exterior-support expansion** ([source](#stmt-n3-domains-support-definition)): Let $(N^d,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold, $d\in\{3,4\}$, with a smooth symmetric tensor $Q$. Let $D\subset N$ be closed, and let $x\in\partial D$ be an interior point of $N$. A smooth exterior support is a smooth function $\phi$ near $x$ with $\phi(x)=0$, $\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$, and $D\subset\{\phi\leq0\}$ locally near $x$. Its normal is $n=\nabla\phi/\|\nabla\phi\|$. Define $$\label{n3:domains:test-expansion} \mathcal E_Q[\phi](x) =\frac{(g^{ij}-n^in^j)\nabla_i\nabla_j\phi}{\|\nabla\phi\|} +\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}Q-Q(n,n).$$ We say $D$ has exterior-support expansion at most $c$ if every such support at every point of its frontier has $\mathcal E_Q[\phi]\leq c$.
