 \qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0.$$ There is a smooth positive function $\rho$, equal to a positive constant times $r^{-4}$ on the far end and satisfying symbol derivative bounds there, such that, for every $h\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$\label{n3:domains:offset-smallness}
 |(h+C)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|+|\nabla C|+\rho
      \leq\tfrac12\mathfrak m
 \quad\hbox{everywhere on }\Omega.$$ The thresholds, collars, offset, and $\rho$ are fixed before the deformation parameters are chosen. After fixing the thresholds and collars, the offset and its first derivatives can be made arbitrarily small.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-domains-prepared-domain</summary>

*Proof.* The large-sphere comparison above confines all negative-threshold regions to a fixed compact set, independently of how close the thresholds are to zero. Choose a slightly larger compact set $\mathcal K$ containing this range and $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}K$ in its interior. Let $$m_0=\min_{\mathcal K}\mathfrak m>0,
 \qquad T_0=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|.$$ First restrict both negative thresholds to an interval so close to zero that $$\max\{|c_b|,|c_w|\}\,T_0<m_0/8,$$ while retaining Equation <a href="#n3:domains:black-interval" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:black-interval">[n3:domains:black-interval]</a>. Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:right-continuity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:right-continuity">6</a> allows the required successive choices in that interval. Construct the two regions, select $\Omega$, and fix their disjoint collars inside $\mathcal K$ as above. All ensuing constants may depend on these fixed choices.

Here is an explicit offset construction. On each collar choose a smooth nonincreasing cutoff $\chi(s)$, equal to one near $s=0$ and zero near the collar’s far end. Choose $\kappa_B>0$ so that $1-\kappa_Bs>0$ throughout that collar. For a common amplitude $a>0$, define the contribution of a black collar to be $a\chi(s)(1-\kappa_Bs)$, and that of a white collar to be $-a\chi(s)(1-\kappa_Bs)$. Extend by zero outside the disjoint collars and sum. This produces a smooth function on the manifold with boundary $\Omega$, supported in $\mathcal K$, with $C_b=a$, $C_w=-a$, and $k_B=a\kappa_B$ on the respective collars. These remain valid bounds when a type is absent. Its $C^1$ norm tends to zero with $a$, even though the collar widths have already been fixed.

For $h\in[b_-,b_+]$ and $C\in[C_w,C_b]$, $$|h+C|\leq\max\{|c_b|,|c_w|\}+C_b-C_w.$$ Choose $a$ so small that $(C_b-C_w)T_0+\|\nabla C\|_\infty<m_0/8$. The first two terms of Equation <a href="#n3:domains:offset-smallness" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:offset-smallness">[n3:domains:offset-smallness]</a> are then at most $m_0/4$ on $\mathcal K$ and vanish outside $\mathcal K$. Finally take a fixed smooth positive weight equal to $r^{-4}$ far out and multiply it by a sufficiently small positive constant. The end lower bound for $\mathfrak m$ and $\delta<1$, together with compact positivity, allow the choice $\rho\leq\mathfrak m/4$ everywhere. This proves Equation <a href="#n3:domains:offset-smallness" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:offset-smallness">[n3:domains:offset-smallness]</a>. All remaining assertions were proved in constructing the regions and collars. ◻

</details>

At the assigned face heights the quantity $h+C$ consequently has the useful exact values <a id="n3:domains:compatible-face-values"></a>$$\label{n3:domains:compatible-face-values}
 \begin{aligned}
  h+C&=c_b=P_B+H&&\text{on }B_b\text{ when }h=b_-,\\
  h+C&=-c_w=P_B-H&&\text{on }B_w\text{ when }h=b_+.
 \end{aligned}$$ These identities determine the deformation’s boundary signs. Right-continuity and Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">10</a> will exclude limiting sublevel sets away from the corresponding full trapped regions.

<a id="n3:deformation:section"></a>
### The elliptic deformation and exclusion of the floor

<a id="n3:deformation:face-thresholds"></a>
We define the coupled system, derive its scalar-curvature identity, and choose a continuation path along which the conformal factor cannot touch its lower bound. We use the fixed data of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">11</a>. Thus $\Omega$ has one controlled asymptotically flat end, $K$ is compactly supported, and its compact boundary $B=B_b\cup B_w$ consists of black and white faces. Either type may be absent. The normal $\nu$ points into $\Omega$, and $$H=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_B\nu,\qquad P_B=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_BK.$$ The numbers $b_-<0<b_+$, the smooth compactly supported offset $C$, and the positive function $\rho=O(r^{-4})$ are fixed as in that proposition. In particular, $$\label{n3:deformation:face-thresholds}
 b_-+C=P_B+H\ \hbox{on }B_b,\qquad
 b_++C=P_B-H\ \hbox{on }B_w.$$ All compact sets and geometric constants in this section are fixed after this preparation. Extend the end radius to a smooth function on $\overline\Omega$ bounded below by one. Write $\Omega_R$ for the large spherical truncations and $S_R$ for their outer boundary.

A *polynomial constant* is bounded by $C(1+N)^A$, with $C,A$ depending on the prepared data and fixed auxiliary profiles, but not on $R$, the homotopy parameter, or the solution. Constants permitted to depend arbitrarily on fixed $N$ will be identified explicitly. First fix $0<\epsilon<1$, then choose $N$ sufficiently large, and finally require $R\ge R_{\min}(N,\epsilon)$. We always take $N\ge4$ and $N>2/\epsilon$.

<a id="n3:deformation:variables"></a>
#### Variables and equations

Choose a smooth nonincreasing $\vartheta:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ equal to one on $(-\infty,0]$ and zero on $[1,\infty)$. Define <a id="n3:deformation:l-profile"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:l-profile}
 \begin{gathered}
 p(t)=N\vartheta(Nt),\qquad
 l(t)=\exp\left(\int_0^t p(s)\,\mathrm ds\right),\\
 L(t)=l(t)e^{2t},\qquad p_L=p+2.
 \end{gathered}$$ Thus $l(0)=1$, $l(t)=e^{Nt}$ for $t\le0$, and $l$ is constant for $t\ge1/N$. Derivatives of $p$ of every fixed order are polynomially bounded. Set <a id="n3:deformation:small-parameters"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:small-parameters}
 \ell=e^{-\epsilon N},\qquad \tau=\ell^{3/2}.$$ Whenever $t\ge-\epsilon$, one has $\ell\le l(t)\le e$.

<a id="n3:deformation:axial-matrices"></a>
For a function $f$, set <a id="n3:deformation:basic-variables"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:basic-variables}
 \begin{gathered}
 \sigma=|\nabla f|,\quad D=1+l^2\sigma^2,\quad d=D^{-1},\\
 a=l\sigma/\sqrt D,\quad v=a^2=1-d,\quad
 w=l\nabla f/\sqrt D,\quad \chi=4d/(4+pv),\\
 Z=t+\tfrac18\log D,\quad u=L\sqrt D,\quad U=l\sqrt D,\quad h=\tau f.
 \end{gathered}$$ Derivatives and contractions refer to $g$ unless indicated otherwise. At $\sigma>0$, write $e=\nabla f/\sigma$ and $A_j=I+(j-1)e\otimes e$. The matrices used below have the direction-free expressions $$\label{n3:deformation:axial-matrices}
 A_d=I-w\otimes w,\qquad
 A_\chi=I-\frac{p+4}{4+pv}w\otimes w.$$ Vectors and covectors are identified with $g$.

<a id="n3:deformation:trace"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:flux"></a>
The unknowns will be $(f,Z)$. For fixed $\nabla f$, $\partial Z/\partial t=1+pv/4>0$, and its defining expression tends to $-\infty$ and $+\infty$ at the two ends of the $t$-axis. It therefore defines a unique smooth $t=t(Z,\nabla f)$ for all inputs, without a floor assumption. The coefficients $t,d,v,w,\chi,u,U$ and the direction-free matrices are smooth at $\nabla f=0$; occurrences of $\sigma$ and $a$ in the equations combine into smooth invariant expressions. One has $0<\chi\le d\le1$ for finite inputs. Define <a id="n3:deformation:metrics"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:metrics}
 \bar g=g+l^2\,\mathrm df^2,\qquad \hat g=e^{4t}\bar g,\qquad
 H^f=\frac l{\sqrt D}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f,\qquad S=K+H^f.$$ The original trace equation is $$\label{n3:deformation:trace}
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}S=F,\qquad F=h+C,$$ where $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_A S$ is contraction with the contravariant matrix $A$. Along the continuation path we will specify modified right sides $F$. The full flux is $$\label{n3:deformation:flux}
 V=uA_\chi\bigl(4\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot)\bigr).$$ Here $f$ is the graph height, while $Z$ combines the conformal variable $t$ with the logarithm of the graph slope. The numbers $d$ and $\chi$ record ellipticity in the gradient direction, and $u$ weights the divergence flux. The scaled height $h=\tau f$ makes the prescribed trace strictly increasing in $f$. At $S_R$ prescribe $f=Z=0$. Initially the inner Dirichlet values are $h=b_-$ on $B_b$ and $h=b_+$ on $B_w$.

<a id="pm-h-19"></a>
#### The exact scalar-curvature identity

The graph-curvature strategy originates in Jang’s equation and the Schoen–Yau positive-energy argument (Jang 1978; Schoen and Yau 1981) <a id="pm-cite-35"></a>[[Jang1978](#ref-Jang1978), [SchoenYau1981](#ref-SchoenYau1981)]. Its generalized warped-graph form and Penrose coupling were developed by Bray and Khuri (Bray and Khuri 2010, 2011) <a id="pm-cite-36"></a>[[BrayKhuri2010](#ref-BrayKhuri2010), [BrayKhuri2011](#ref-BrayKhuri2011)]; see in particular Identity 9 of (Bray and Khuri 2011) <a id="pm-cite-37"></a>[[BrayKhuri2011](#ref-BrayKhuri2011)]. We use the independently proved algebraic identity of (OpenAI 2026b, Proposition 4.1) <a id="pm-cite-38"></a>[[NumericalCompanion](#ref-NumericalCompanion)], with the normalization below. The prescribed trace $F=h+C$, nonzero source, and floor penalty below define a different coupled system; the identity does not import global solvability of a zero-divergence coupling.

The next identity separates the original constraint densities, a nonnegative quadratic term, and a divergence. The second equation will prescribe that divergence so that the deformed metric has nonnegative scalar curvature.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-identity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:identity" class="proposition">

<a id="n3:deformation:scalar-identity"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:quadratic-term"></a>
**Proposition 12** (Deformation identity). *Let $f,t$ be smooth and $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}(K+H^f)$. At $\sigma>0$ decompose $S$ relative to $\mathbb Re\oplus e^\perp$: $$T=S|_{e^\perp\times e^\perp},\quad
 M=S(e,\cdot)|_{e^\perp},\quad q=S(e,e),\quad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}T=F-\chi q.$$ Then $$\label{n3:deformation:scalar-identity}
 \begin{split}
 \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g}
 ={}&8\pi(\mu+J(w))+\mathcal T
       +w(F)-F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V,
 \end{split}$$ where $$\label{n3:deformation:quadratic-term}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2
 +(M+pa\nabla_\perp t)\cdot(M+(p+2)a\nabla_\perp t)\\
 &+4(p+1)|\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2
   +(\chi-\chi^2/4)q^2+2(p+1)\chi qa\,\partial_e t\\
 &-\chi Fq/2+3F^2/4.
 \end{split}$$ After substituting $F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}S$, this expression extends smoothly across $\sigma=0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-identity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-identity</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary"></a>
*Proof.* Apply the scalar identity of (OpenAI 2026b, Proposition 4.1) <a id="pm-cite-39"></a>[[NumericalCompanion](#ref-NumericalCompanion)] in spatial dimension three, so its surface dimension is $k=2$. To distinguish the two conventions temporarily, add a subscript $\mathrm A$ to its variables. The exact dictionary is $$\label{n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary}
 \begin{gathered}
 t_{\mathrm A}=2t,\quad Z_{\mathrm A}=2Z,\quad
 l_{\mathrm A}(s)=l(s/2),\quad p_{\mathrm A}=p/2,\\
 \mu_{\mathrm A}=8\pi\mu,\qquad J_{\mathrm A}=8\pi J,
 \qquad S_{\mathrm A}=S.
 \end{gathered}$$ The quantities $D,d,w,a,v,H^f,F,U$ are identical. In particular, $$\frac{2d}{2+p_{\mathrm A}v}=\frac{4d}{4+pv}=\chi,
 \quad u_{\mathrm A}=e^{t_{\mathrm A}}l\sqrt D=u,
 \quad 2\nabla Z_{\mathrm A}=4\nabla Z,$$ and the companion metric $e^{2t_{\mathrm A}}\bar g$ is precisely $\hat g=e^{4t}\bar g$. Thus the divergence term, trace prescription and metric match without rescaling their flux. The physical density conversion gives $8\pi(\mu+J(w))$; the ADM energy and momentum are not changed by that conversion.

For the quadratic expression, the companion coefficient $s_p=p_{\mathrm A}+(k-1)/2$ is $(p+1)/2$, and $dt_{\mathrm A}=2dt$. Its transverse square is $|M+(p+1)a\nabla_\perp t|^2$. Combining its residual $-[a^2|\nabla_\perp t|^2]$ with that square gives $(M+pa\nabla_\perp t)\cdot(M+(p+2)a\nabla_\perp t)$. The remaining gradient contribution is $4(p+1)|dt|_{A_d}^2$. Its normal terms become $$(\chi-\chi^2/4)q^2+2(p+1)\chi qa\,\partial_e t
       -\chi Fq/2+3F^2/4.$$ These substitutions give Equations <a href="#n3:deformation:scalar-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:scalar-identity">[n3:deformation:scalar-identity]</a> and <a href="#n3:deformation:quadratic-term" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:quadratic-term">[n3:deformation:quadratic-term]</a>. Smoothness at zero gradient is part of the invariant identity: the temporary axis has not been used to define its coefficients. The import is pointwise and requires neither an energy condition nor a solved divergence equation. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:coercivity" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:coercive-estimate"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-norm"></a>
**Lemma 13** (Polynomial coercivity). *The weighted coercivity theorem of (OpenAI 2026b, Proposition 4.2) <a id="pm-cite-40"></a>[[NumericalCompanion](#ref-NumericalCompanion)], with Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary">[n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary]</a>, makes $\mathcal T$ nonnegative. For $0\le p\le N$, $$\label{n3:deformation:coercive-estimate}
 |\,\mathrm dt|_{A_d}^2+|T|^2+|M|^2+dq^2+F^2
 \le C(1+N)^A\mathcal T$$ with universal $C,A$. At $\,\mathrm dt=0$ there is the stronger comparison, uniform in $p,d$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-norm}
 c\bigl(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+|M|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr)
 \le\mathcal T
 \le C\bigl(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+|M|^2+\chi q^2+F^2\bigr).$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-coercivity</summary>

*Proof.* With $x=\partial_e t$ and $y=\nabla_\perp t$, exact completion gives <a id="n3:deformation:square-completion"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:square-completion}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2
 +|M+(p+1)ay|^2+[4(p+1)-v]|y|^2\\
 &+4(p+1)d\left(x+\frac{\chi aq}{4d}\right)^2\\
 &+\tfrac34\left(F-\frac{\chi q}{3}\right)^2
 +\frac{4d(9-d)}{3(4+pv)^2}q^2.
 \end{split}$$ Completing first in $x$ leaves $3\chi q^2/(4+pv)$; completing next in $F$ leaves $3\chi/(4+pv)-\chi^2/12=4d(9-d)/[3(4+pv)^2]$. The latter coefficient is at least $32d/[3(4+N)^2]$. It controls $dq^2$ polynomially. The $F$-square then controls $F^2$, since $\chi^2q^2\le dq^2$. The transverse gradient coefficient is at least three, and the shifted $M$-square controls $M$ with an additional factor $(1+N)^2$. The squared $d$-norm of the shift in the $x$-square is $\chi^2vq^2/(16d)\le dq^2/16$, so it also controls $dx^2$. Finally $|T|^2=|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+(F-\chi q)^2/2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:coercive-estimate" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:coercive-estimate">[n3:deformation:coercive-estimate]</a>. If $\,\mathrm dt=0$, the sole cross term is $-\chi Fq/2$. Using $|\chi Fq|/2\le\chi q^2/4+\chi F^2/4$ and $0<\chi\le1$ proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="n3:deformation:Z-differential"></a>
The scalar identity separates curvature from divergence. At the inner boundary we must also relate this divergence flux to mean curvature. Differentiating the definition of $Z$ gives, wherever $df\ne0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:Z-differential}
 4\,dt+\tfrac12\,d\log D
       =4\,dZ=(4+pv)\,dt+v\,d\log\sigma.$$ This relation is smooth in its direction-free form and will be used only in contractions that extend across $df=0$.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:boundary-identity" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:boundary"></a>
**Lemma 14** (Boundary identity). *On a face where $f$ is constant, $$\label{n3:deformation:boundary}
 V_\nu/u=d(H+4\partial_\nu t)-H+w_\nu(F-P_B).$$ Its mean curvature in $\hat g$, with normal into $\Omega$, is $e^{-2t}\sqrt d\,(H+4\partial_\nu t)$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-boundary-identity</summary>

*Proof.* The tangential Hessian is $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f|_{TB}=(\partial_\nu f)\operatorname{II}_g$. Thus $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp H^f=w_\nu H$ and $\chi q=F-P_B-w_\nu H$. The normal component of <a href="#n3:deformation:flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:flux">[n3:deformation:flux]</a>, using <a href="#n3:deformation:Z-differential" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:Z-differential">[n3:deformation:Z-differential]</a>, is $$V_\nu/u=4d\partial_\nu t+\chi w_\nu q
        =4d\partial_\nu t+w_\nu(F-P_B)-vH.$$ The $\bar g$-normal is $\sqrt d\,\nu$. Its mean curvature is $\sqrt d\,H$, because the tangential metric is unchanged and its normal first variation is multiplied by $\sqrt d$. The conformal mean-curvature formula gives the asserted mean curvature for $\hat g$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-20"></a>
#### The source, boundary condition, and continuation path

We now prescribe the divergence and inner flux. For the original system, the source is chosen to give the deformed metric nonnegative scalar curvature. A penalty near the lower bound will exclude contact with that bound along the continuation path.

<a id="n3:deformation:source"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:original-second-equation"></a>
Choose $3/4<\gamma<1$ and fixed positive smooth weights $$\rho_0\asymp r^{-4},\qquad \rho_1\asymp r^{-2\gamma},$$ with differentiated end bounds. Let $m:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be smooth, equal to one on $(-\infty,0]$ and zero on $[1,\infty)$, and set $$m_0(t)=m(N(t+\epsilon)),\qquad
 \mathcal P=C_N(\rho_0+v\rho_1).$$ The positive $\delta_0$ is fixed independently of $N,R$ in Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor">20</a>; thereafter $C_N$ is a sufficiently large polynomial constant. Define $$\label{n3:deformation:source}
 \Xi=\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+\delta_0\tau a\sigma-m_0(t)\mathcal P.$$ Choose a smooth face function $N_B>1+\sup_B|H|$. The original second equation and its inner condition are $$\label{n3:deformation:original-second-equation}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}V=u\Xi,\qquad V_\nu/u=-H+w_\nu(F-P_B)-N_Bd.$$ Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:boundary-identity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:boundary-identity">14</a> gives $H+4\partial_\nu t=-N_B$. Only $-\epsilon\le t\le-\epsilon+1/N$ is penalized in the admissible range. Since $N>2/\epsilon$, this band has negative $t$, and <a id="n3:deformation:penalty-band"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:penalty-band}
 \ell\le l\le e\ell,\qquad c\ell\le L\le C\ell
 \quad\hbox{on the admissible penalty band}.$$ The latter constants can be uniform for $0<\epsilon<1$.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:homotopy" class="proposition">

**Proposition 15** (Specified homotopy). *There is a continuous piecewise smooth family of systems indexed by $s\in[0,4]$, beginning at <a href="#n3:deformation:trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:trace">[n3:deformation:trace]</a>, <a href="#n3:deformation:original-second-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:original-second-equation">[n3:deformation:original-second-equation]</a> and the original Dirichlet values, and ending at $f=0$ and the scalar problem with zero source and zero inner conormal flux. Throughout its first three stages the source is <a href="#n3:deformation:source" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:source">[n3:deformation:source]</a>, with $\mathcal T$ evaluated using the actual trace $F$. Each trace equation has right-side derivative at least one in $h$, with $x,Z,\nabla f$ fixed.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-homotopy</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary"></a>
*Proof.* Fix a smooth $j:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ which vanishes for $t\le0$ and equals one for $t\ge1$. For $0\le\lambda\le1$ put $$V_\lambda=uA_\chi(4\nabla Z+\lambda K(w,\cdot)),\qquad
 \mathcal B=-H+w_\nu(F-P_B)-N_Bd.$$ Before the last stage use the boundary condition $$\label{n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary}
 \begin{split}
 (V_\lambda)_\nu/u
 ={}&[1-(1-\lambda)j(t)]\\
 &\cdot[\mathcal B-(1-\lambda)(A_\chi K(w,\cdot))_\nu].
 \end{split}$$ Outer values remain $f=Z=0$ throughout.

We specify two smooth collar modifications. Let $\nu_s=\nabla s/|\nabla s|$ be the outward unit normal to a collar leaf; the leaf coordinate $s$ here is local and is separate from the homotopy parameter. Choose disjoint collar cutoffs equal to one at the faces. Take $\eta>0$ so small that $b_-+3\eta<b_+$. A black contribution to $D_0(x,w,h)$ is a negative constant times a collar cutoff, times a smooth directional cutoff supported where $w\cdot\nu_s<-1/2$ and equal to one at $-1$, times a nonincreasing height cutoff equal to one below $b_-+\eta$ and zero above $b_-+2\eta$. A white contribution has positive sign, its directional cutoff supported where $w\cdot\nu_s>1/2$ and equal to one at $1$, and a nondecreasing height cutoff equal to zero below $b_+-2\eta$ and one above $b_+-\eta$. Decrease $\eta$ to separate these ranges. Their sum $D_0$ is smooth, bounded, supported in the collars, and nondecreasing in $h$. It is nonpositive for $h\le b_-+\eta$, nonnegative for $h\ge b_+-\eta$, and vanishes on black outward and white inward directions, for every length $0\le|w|\le1$.

<a id="n3:deformation:directional-barriers"></a>
Choose the magnitudes larger than $2\sup_B|H|+1$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:face-thresholds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:face-thresholds">[n3:deformation:face-thresholds]</a> then gives, for $F=h+C+D_0$ at the assigned boundary height $b=b_\pm$, $$\label{n3:deformation:directional-barriers}
 F(x,+\nu,b)\ge P_B+H,\qquad F(x,-\nu,b)\le P_B-H.$$ These are limiting directional evaluations at $a=1,\chi=0$. The compatible direction has equality; $D_0$ corrects the other one. Its derivatives on bounded height ranges are independent of $N$. Choose a smooth compactly supported extension $b(x)$, constant equal to $b_\pm$ on each smaller collar. On these collars let $D_1(x,w)=A_1w\cdot\nu_s$, extended by a collar cutoff, with $A_1>\sup_B|H|+1$. Then $D_1(x,0)=0$ and $D_1(x,\pm\nu)=\pm A_1$ on $B$.

The four stages are the following.

1.  For $0\le s\le1$, set $\lambda=1-s$, keep $F=h+C$ and $h|_B=b$, and use $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda=u\Xi$ and <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a>.

2.  For $1\le s\le2$, set $\lambda=0$, $\alpha=s-1$, retain $h|_B=b$, and replace the trace right side by $F=h+C+\alpha D_0(x,w,h)$. Keep the same scalar equation and boundary prescription.

3.  For $2\le s\le3$, set $\lambda=0$, $\zeta=s-2$, prescribe $h|_B=(1-\zeta)b$, and use <a id="n3:deformation:interpolation-trace"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:interpolation-trace}
     \begin{split}
     F={}&h+(1-\zeta)[C+D_0(x,w,h+\zeta b(x))]\\
        &+\zeta[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}K+D_1(x,w)].
     \end{split}$$ Keep the same scalar equation and boundary prescription. At a face, $h+\zeta b=b$. The value at $w=\pm\nu$ is the convex combination of the preceding directional value and $P_B+D_1(x,\pm\nu)$, so <a href="#n3:deformation:directional-barriers" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:directional-barriers">[n3:deformation:directional-barriers]</a> persists.

4.  For $3\le s\le4$, retain the trace problem at $\zeta=1$ and multiply both $\Xi$ and the right side of <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a> by $\eta_s=4-s$.

The prescriptions agree at the common endpoints. Their $h$-derivatives are $1$, $1+\alpha\partial_hD_0$, or $1+(1-\zeta)\partial_hD_0$, all at least one.

At $\zeta=1$ the trace equation is $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}H^f=h+D_1(x,w)$ with zero Dirichlet values. At a positive interior maximum of $f$, one has $w=0$, $A_\chi=I$, $D_1=0$, and $l\Delta f=\tau f>0$, a contradiction. A negative minimum is excluded in the same way. Thus $f=0$ and $t=Z$ in the last stage. At $s=4$ the remaining equation is $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(4L(Z)\nabla Z)=0$, with zero inner conormal flux and $Z=0$ on $S_R$. Multiplication by $Z$ and integration give $Z=0$. For the fixed-point construction in Section <a href="#n3:existence:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:existence:section">6</a>, the final linear scalar problem has zero source and zero inner flux for every input; consequently that last map has output identically zero. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-21"></a>
#### Elementary height and end barriers

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-height"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:height" class="lemma">

**Lemma 16** (Height control). *Every smooth trace solution in Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a> satisfies $|h|\le C_0$, independently of $N,R$, the homotopy parameter, and the input $Z$. Its actual right side satisfies $|F|\le C_F$ with the same independence.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-height"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-height</summary>

*Proof.* The collar modifications vanish at $w=0$. At an interior extremum the trace equation reads either $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+l\Delta f=h+C$ or $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+l\Delta f=h+(1-\zeta)C+\zeta\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K$. The maximum and minimum inequalities bound $h$ by fixed bounds for $|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K|+|C|$. Boundary values range between $b_-,0,b_+$. This proves the height bound without using the floor. Boundedness of $D_0,D_1$ and $|\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}K|\le3|K|$ proves the assertion for $F$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-end-height"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:end-height" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:outer-gradient"></a>
**Lemma 17** (End height and outer boundary). *There are $r_0,C>0$, independent of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameter, such that for $R\ge2r_0$, <a id="n3:deformation:end-height-estimate"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:end-height-estimate}
 |h|\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R^{-\gamma})\quad(r_0\le r\le R).$$ In particular, $$\label{n3:deformation:outer-gradient}
 |\nabla f|\le C R^{-1-\gamma}/\tau\quad\hbox{on }S_R.$$ For fixed $\epsilon,N$, a sufficiently large lower bound for $R$ gives $t>-\epsilon$ on $S_R$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-end-height"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-end-height</summary>

*Proof.* Take $r_0$ outside the supports of $K,C,D_0,D_1$. There $F=h$ in the first three stages, and $h=0$ in the last one. For $\psi=r^{-\gamma}$, with axis $\nabla\psi/|\nabla\psi|$, the controlled end gives, uniformly for $0<\chi\le1$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\psi
 =\gamma((\gamma+1)\chi-2)r^{-\gamma-2}
      +O(r^{-\gamma-3})<0$$ after enlarging $r_0$. At a comparison contact, coefficients use the given $Z$ and the common gradient of test and solution. The positive factor $l/(\tau\sqrt D)$ preserves this sign. Height monotonicity therefore makes $C(\psi-R^{-\gamma})$ an upper barrier and its negative a lower barrier. Choose $C$ to dominate $C_0$ on $r=r_0$ for every $R\ge2r_0$. Differentiating at the common outer value gives <a href="#n3:deformation:outer-gradient" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:outer-gradient">[n3:deformation:outer-gradient]</a>; tangential derivatives there vanish.

At $S_R$, $Z=0$. The monotonicity of its defining expression implies $t>-\epsilon$ if $\ell^2|\nabla f|^2<e^{8\epsilon}-1$. It suffices to require $C^2\ell^2\tau^{-2}R^{-2-2\gamma}<e^{8\epsilon}-1$, which is a permissible lower bound depending on fixed $N,\epsilon$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-22"></a>
#### Exclusion of a contact with the floor

We exclude a proposed floor contact using the equations at that point. These estimates require neither an upper bound for $Z$ nor a bound for $|\nabla f|$.

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor-curvature" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-gauss"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general"></a>
<a id="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end"></a>
**Lemma 18** (Curvature at a minimum of $t$). *At an interior point where $\,\mathrm dt=0$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}t\ge0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-gauss}
 \tfrac12e^{4t}\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\hat g}
 \le \tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)+\mathcal S(H^f),$$ where, for a symmetric tensor $A$, $$\label{n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal S(A)={}&\tfrac14(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A)^2
 -\tfrac12|A_{\perp\perp}^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2\\
 &+dA_{ee}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A-d|A_{e\perp}|^2.
 \end{split}$$ There are universal $c_*,\eta_*>0$ and polynomial constants $C_N$ such that, at $\,\mathrm dt=0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)
 \ge c_*\mathcal T-C_N(F^2+|K|^2).$$ If $K=0$, the more useful uniform estimate is $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)\ge c_*\mathcal T-C_N vF^2.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor-curvature</summary>

*Proof.* Consider the graph of $f$ in the Riemannian product with warped fiber $(\Omega\times\mathbb R,g+l^2\,\mathrm db_0^2)$. Its induced metric is $\bar g$. At $\,\mathrm dt=0$ one also has $\,\mathrm dl=0$, and its second fundamental form, up to orientation, is $H^f$. Write $E=l^{-1}\partial_{b_0}$. The graph unit normal is $\sqrt d\,E-ae$. The ambient curvature formulas at this point are $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\mathrm{amb}}=\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-2\Delta l/l,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathrm{amb}}|_{T\Omega}=\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g-\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l/l,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathrm{amb}}(E,E)=-\Delta l/l,
 \end{gathered}$$ with zero mixed Ricci terms. Hence the ambient contribution to half the graph scalar curvature is $$\tfrac12\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)
      -v\,\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l/l.$$ The last term is nonpositive: at $\,\mathrm dt=0$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}l=lp\,\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}t$ and $p\ge0$. The second-form contribution is $[(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{\bar g}H^f)^2-|H^f|_{\bar g}^2]/2$. Since the inverse graph metric is $A_d$, its expansion is exactly <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a>. Finally the conformal contribution at this point is $-4\bar\Delta t\le0$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-gauss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-gauss">[n3:deformation:floor-gauss]</a>.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-difference"></a>
The pointwise algebraic clause of (OpenAI 2026b, Lemma 4.3) <a id="pm-cite-41"></a>[[NumericalCompanion](#ref-NumericalCompanion)] applies under Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary">[n3:deformation:normalization-dictionary]</a>. We also record its three-dimensional calculation, because the boundary homotopy below needs its precise degenerate normal coefficient. First evaluate $\mathcal S$ on $S=K+H^f$, whose trace in the transverse plane is $F-\chi q$. Subtracting <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a> from <a href="#n3:deformation:quadratic-term" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:quadratic-term">[n3:deformation:quadratic-term]</a> at $\,\mathrm dt=0$ gives $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-difference}
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal T-\mathcal S(S)
 ={}&|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|^2+(1+d)|M|^2\\
 &+\chi(1+d-\chi/2)q^2-dFq+F^2/2.
 \end{split}$$ The normal coefficient is at least $\chi$, while $|dFq|\le\chi q^2/2+d^2F^2/(2\chi)$. Because $$d^2/\chi=d(4+pv)/4\le1+N/4,$$ Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> implies $\mathcal T-\mathcal S(S)\ge c\mathcal T-C(1+N)F^2$ with universal $c>0$.

To replace $S$ by $H^f=S-K$, polarize <a href="#n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic">[n3:deformation:gauss-quadratic]</a>. The difference is bounded by $$C|K|(|T^{\operatorname{tf}}|+|M|+|F|+d|q|)+C|K|^2.$$ Indeed the only extra normal product is $dq\,\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp K$; all remaining products involve transverse entries, $dM$, or $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp S=F-\chi q$. By <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> and $d/\sqrt\chi\le C\sqrt{1+N}$, this bound is at most $C\sqrt{1+N}|K|\sqrt{\mathcal T}+C|K|^2$. Young’s inequality absorbs a fixed small fraction of $\mathcal T$ and costs only $C(1+N)|K|^2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a>.

If $(1+p)v\le\eta_*$, then $d$ and $\chi$ are within $C\eta_*$ of one. At $d=\chi=1$ the normal block in <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-difference" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-difference">[n3:deformation:floor-difference]</a> is $3q^2/2-Fq+F^2/2$; its symmetric matrix has smallest eigenvalue $(2-\sqrt2)/2>0$. Choose $\eta_*>0$ small enough that its coefficients remain within half this spectral gap. The transverse coefficients are already bounded below. For $K=0$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> therefore gives $\mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f)\ge c_*\mathcal T$ in this regime. In the remaining regime $v>\eta_* /(1+p)$, use <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a> with $K=0$ and absorb $(1+N)F^2$ into $C(1+N)^2vF^2$. This proves <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end]</a>. All formulas extend to $\sigma=0$ by their invariant expressions; there $d=\chi=1$ and the full quadratic expressions are independent of the temporary choice of axis. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor-errors" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower"></a>
**Lemma 19** (Homotopy errors at a floor contact). *There is a fixed compact set $\mathcal K\subset\overline\Omega$ containing the supports of $K,C,b,D_0,D_1$ such that, at an interior minimum $t=-\epsilon$ of a smooth solution in the first three stages, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda/u
 \ge 2\delta_0\mathcal T+\tau a\sigma
      -C(1+N)^A
       [\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+v(\rho_0+\rho_1)].$$ Here $\delta_0>0$ can be fixed sufficiently small independently of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameter.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor-errors</summary>

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-w-control"></a>
*Proof.* At this contact $\,\mathrm dt=0$ and $p=N$ is locally constant as a function of $t$ near its value $-\epsilon$. Differentiating $w$ in an orthonormal frame gives <a id="n3:deformation:floor-w-derivative"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:floor-w-derivative}
 \nabla_iw_j=H^f_{ij}-w_jH^f_{ik}w^k.$$ In the $e$-frame the normal vector slot is multiplied by $d$. Equations <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a> and $d/\sqrt\chi\le C\sqrt{1+N}$ therefore show $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-w-control}
 |\nabla w|\le C(1+N)^A(|K|+\sqrt{\mathcal T}).$$ No bound for the uncontracted normal Hessian is asserted.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-F-control"></a>
Each first-three-stage right side can be written as a smooth function $F(x,w,h,p)$. Its $h$-derivative is at least one. On the bounded height range supplied by Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">16</a>, its explicit $x$- and $w$-derivatives are polynomially bounded and compactly supported, apart from the derivative of the term $h$. This follows directly from the fixed collar cutoffs and $A_\chi=I-(p+4)w\otimes w/(4+pv)$, whose denominator is at least four. For example its first $w$-derivatives on $|w|\le1$ are bounded by $C(1+N)^2$, and the other explicit modifications have bounds independent of $N$. Combining these bounds with <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a> and Young’s inequality therefore produces a fixed finite power of $1+N$. Since $\nabla p=0$ at the contact and $w(h)=\tau a\sigma$, the chain rule and <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a> give, for every fixed $\eta>0$, $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-F-control}
 w(F)\ge\tau a\sigma-\eta\mathcal T
                 -C_\eta(1+N)^A\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}.$$ The dependence $D_0(x,w,h+\zeta b(x))$ only adds the fixed compact derivative of $b$ and does not change this conclusion.

<a id="n3:deformation:floor-flux-control"></a>
The omitted flux is $(1-\lambda)uA_\chi K(w,\cdot)$. Let $B_K=A_\chi K(w,\cdot)$. Its derivative is bounded by a polynomial constant times $1+\sqrt{\mathcal T}$ on $\mathcal K$, by <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-w-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-w-control">[n3:deformation:floor-w-control]</a>; derivatives of $p$ vanish. The weight term requires the contraction rather than a bound for $|\nabla\log u|$. At the contact, $$\nabla\log u=H^f(w,\cdot),\qquad
 \langle\nabla\log u,B_K\rangle
 =a^2\bigl(\chi H^f_{ee}K_{ee}
                    +H^f_{e\perp}\cdot K_{e\perp}\bigr).$$ This involves only $\chi H^f_{ee}$ and $H^f_{e\perp}$ and is controlled by <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-norm" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-norm">[n3:deformation:floor-norm]</a>. It follows that $$\label{n3:deformation:floor-flux-control}
 |\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uB_K)|/u
 \le\eta\mathcal T+C_\eta(1+N)^A\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}.$$

Combine the scalar identity with <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-gauss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-gauss">[n3:deformation:floor-gauss]</a>. The difference $8\pi\mu-\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_g/2$ equals $((\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K)^2-|K|^2)/2$ and is compactly supported; so is $J$. The term $F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K$ is compactly bounded by Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">16</a>. On $\mathcal K$, Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-general]</a> therefore contributes $c_*\mathcal T-C(1+N)^A$. Outside $\mathcal K$, $K=0$, $F=h$, and <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end">[n3:deformation:floor-algebra-end]</a> together with Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">17</a> gives $c_*\mathcal T-C(1+N)^Av r^{-2\gamma}$. The remaining Ricci term is bounded below by $-C\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}-Cv r^{-3}$; enlarge $\mathcal K$ if necessary. Both end weights are bounded by a multiple of $\rho_0+\rho_1$. Finally subtract the omitted flux and use <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-F-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-F-control">[n3:deformation:floor-F-control]</a>–<a href="#n3:deformation:floor-flux-control" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-flux-control">[n3:deformation:floor-flux-control]</a>, choosing their two $\eta$’s with sum at most $c_*/2$. Fix $0<\delta_0<\min(c_*/4,1/4)$. Decreasing it slightly if necessary gives <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower">[n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n3-deformation-floor"></a>
<div id="n3:deformation:floor" class="proposition">

**Proposition 20** (Floor exclusion). *Choose $\delta_0$ as in Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-errors" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-errors">19</a>. There is a polynomial choice $C_N=C(1+N)^A$ in the penalty such that, for all sufficiently large $N$ and all $R\ge R_{\mathrm{floor}}(N,\epsilon)$, no smooth solution anywhere along Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a> can satisfy $t\ge-\epsilon$ and attain $t=-\epsilon$. In particular every such admissible solution has $t>-\epsilon$ on $\overline{\Omega_R}$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-deformation-floor"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-deformation-floor</summary>

*Proof.* Choose $R_{\mathrm{floor}}$ to include the requirement of Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">17</a>. A floor contact cannot occur on $S_R$. In the first three stages, an inner contact has $j(t)=0$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary">[n3:deformation:homotopy-boundary]</a> then cancels the omitted flux on both sides and gives $V_\nu/u=\mathcal B$. Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:boundary">[n3:deformation:boundary]</a> forces $H+4\partial_\nu t=-N_B$, so $\partial_\nu t<0$. This contradicts the nonnegative derivative into $\Omega_R$ at a boundary minimum.

Consider an interior contact. Let $E_N=C(1+N)^A[\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}+v(\rho_0+\rho_1)]$ denote the error in <a href="#n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower">[n3:deformation:floor-divergence-lower]</a>. Because $\rho_0$ has a positive minimum on $\mathcal K$, $\mathbf1_{\mathcal K}\le C_{\mathcal K}\rho_0$. Also $v\rho_0\le\rho_0$, and $\rho/\rho_0$ is globally bounded. We can therefore choose a polynomial $C_N$ so large that, pointwise for all $0\le v\le1$, <a id="n3:deformation:penalty-choice"></a>$$\label{n3:deformation:penalty-choice}
 \mathcal P\ge E_N+2\rho+\rho_0.$$ At the floor $m_0=1$, so the scalar equation and the lower estimate give $$\begin{split}
 0
 &\ge \delta_0\mathcal T+(1-\delta_0)\tau a\sigma
                     +\mathcal P-E_N-\rho\\
 &\ge \rho+\rho_0>0,
 \end{split}$$ a contradiction. Enlarging $C_N$ below preserves this inequality and preserves its polynomial dependence.

In the last stage $f=0$, $t=Z$, $u=L$, and $v=0$. At an interior minimum, $\mathcal T=(|K|^2+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K)^2)/2$. Increase $C_N$ polynomially if necessary so that $\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho-C_N\rho_0<0$ at all such points. For $\eta_s>0$, the scalar equation at a floor minimum has left side $4L\Delta t\ge0$ and strictly negative right side. At an inner floor minimum its flux is $4\partial_\nu t=\eta_s(-H-N_B)<0$, also impossible. If $\eta_s=0$, multiplication of $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(4L(t)\nabla t)=0$ by $t$, with zero outer value and zero inner flux, gives $t=0$. Thus the last stage has no floor contact either. ◻

</details>

We have excluded floor contact for every smooth admissible solution along the specified homotopy. Section <a href="#n3:apriori:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:section">5</a> supplies the remaining a priori bounds, and Section <a href="#n3:existence:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:existence:section">6</a> proves existence. The choice of $\mathcal P$ uses only polynomial losses in $N$; it is independent of all fixed-$N$ Schauder constants.

<a id="n3:apriori:section"></a>
### A priori estimates for the deformation

We bound the height, boundary slopes, and conformal variable before using classical regularity. Fix the prepared exterior of Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">11</a>, its thresholds and collars, and $\epsilon>0$. We use the variables and four stages of Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a>. A solution is smooth on a finite truncation and satisfies $t\ge-\epsilon$, so the estimates include putative floor-contact solutions. No Hessian bound or upper bound for $Z$ is assumed.

<a id="n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons"></a>
A quantity denoted by $\Pi_N$ is bounded by $C(1+N)^A$, with $C,A$ independent of the truncation, the homotopy parameter, and $N$. It can increase at successive uses. The fixed data, collars, and $\epsilon$ can enter $C,A$. A constant denoted by $C(N)$ can depend arbitrarily on these fixed data and on $N,\ell,\tau$; it is still independent of the truncation and the homotopy parameter. Constants explicitly described as fixed do not depend on $N$. Recall that $$\ell=e^{-\epsilon N},\qquad \tau=\ell^{3/2},\qquad
 \ell\le l\le e,\qquad 0\le p\le N,
 \qquad \frac{4d}{4+N}\le\chi\le d.
 \label{n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons}$$ In particular $\Pi_N\tau/\ell\to0$. This small factor will absorb only terms whose constants are polynomial.

<a id="pm-h-24"></a>
#### Sublevels and exclusion of boundary layers

The limiting height will be only lower semicontinuous. We first show how an expansion bound on its lower tests controls every exterior support of a closed sublevel, including a plateau. This local step will also apply to the four-dimensional constructions.

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-sublevel-support"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:sublevel-support" class="lemma">

**Lemma 21** (Exterior supports of a closed sublevel). *Let $U$ be an open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$, let $Q$ be a smooth symmetric tensor on $U$, and let $u:U\to\mathbb R$ be finite and lower semicontinuous. Fix $k<k'$ and $q_0\in\mathbb R$. A smooth lower test of $u$ at $x$ is a smooth function $\phi$ with $\phi(x)=u(x)$ and $\phi\le u$ near $x$. Suppose every such test with $u(x)<k'$ and $\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$ satisfies $$\mathcal E_Q[\phi](x)\le q_0,$$ where $\mathcal E_Q$ is the expansion in Equation <a href="#n3:domains:test-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:domains:test-expansion">[n3:domains:test-expansion]</a> of the regular level through $x$, oriented toward increasing $\phi$. Equivalently, subtract $\phi(x)$ before applying that formula. Then every smooth exterior support of the relatively closed set $D_k=\{x\in U:u(x)\le k\}$, at a frontier point in $U$, has expansion at most $q_0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-sublevel-support"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-sublevel-support</summary>

*Proof.* For integers $j\ge1$ define <a id="n3:apriori:sigmoid"></a>$$\label{n3:apriori:sigmoid}
 S_j(s)=\bigl(1+\exp[-j^2(s-k-j^{-1})]\bigr)^{-1},
 \qquad v_j=S_j\circ u.$$ These functions are lower semicontinuous and take values in $(0,1)$. Their lower relaxed limit $\liminf_{j\to\infty,\,y\to x}v_j(y)$ is the function $I_k(x)$ equal to zero on $D_k$ and one on its complement. Indeed, at $x\in D_k$ the constant sequence gives $v_j(x)\le S_j(k)\to0$, while $v_j\ge0$ everywhere. If $u(x)>k$, lower semicontinuity gives a neighborhood on which $u\ge k+\delta$ for some $\delta>0$, and $v_j\to1$ uniformly there.

Let $\phi$ define an exterior support of $D_k$ at $x$: $\phi(x)=0$, $\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$, and $\phi\le0$ on $D_k$ near $x$. Shrink to a small normal-coordinate ball compactly contained in $U$ on which $|\phi|<1/2$. Then $\phi$ is a lower test of $I_k$ at $x$. Subtract a small positive multiple of the fourth power of the distance from $x$ to make this contact strict without changing its two-jet; write the resulting function as $\phi_0$. Minimize $v_j-\phi_0$ on the closed ball. The preceding relaxed-limit description, the strict contact, and $v_j(x)\to0$ show that the minimizers $x_j$ lie in its interior for large $j$, satisfy $x_j\to x$, and have contact values $v_j(x_j)\to0$. Thus $\phi_0+a_j$ is a lower test of $v_j$ at $x_j$, where $a_j\to0$.

For each fixed large $j$, restrict to a neighborhood of $x_j$ on which $\phi_0+a_j$ takes values in $(0,1)$. The increasing function $S_j^{-1}$ makes $S_j^{-1}(\phi_0+a_j)$ a smooth lower test of $u$. Its contact height is $$u(x_j)=k+j^{-1}
       +j^{-2}\log\frac{v_j(x_j)}{1-v_j(x_j)}
       \le k+j^{-1}<k'$$ for all sufficiently large $j$. Its gradient is nonzero, since $\,\mathrm d\phi_0(x_j)\to\,\mathrm d\phi(x)\ne0$. An increasing smooth composition preserves the oriented level expansion: it preserves the unit normal, and for $\theta'>0$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}(\theta\circ\phi_0)
  =\theta'\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi_0
       +\theta''\,\mathrm d\phi_0\otimes\,\mathrm d\phi_0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(\,\mathrm d\phi_0)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}(\theta\circ\phi_0)}
 {|\,\mathrm d(\theta\circ\phi_0)|}
 =\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(\,\mathrm d\phi_0)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi_0}{|\,\mathrm d\phi_0|}.$$ The hypothesis therefore gives $\mathcal E_Q[\phi_0+a_j](x_j)\le q_0$. Letting $j\to\infty$ yields $\mathcal E_Q[\phi](x)\le q_0$, because $\phi_0$ and $\phi$ have the same two-jet at $x$. ◻

</details>

For notation in this section, let $\mathcal B_c$ be the full closed maximal black region at threshold $c$, and let $\mathcal W_c$ be the corresponding white region with $\mathcal B_{c_b}$ held fixed. These are the families used in Proposition <a href="#n3:domains:prepared-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:prepared-domain">11</a>.

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:sublevels" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:apriori:lower-height"></a>
**Lemma 22** (Uniform separation from the wrong height). *In the first two homotopy stages, the following holds. If $Q\subset\bar\Omega$ is compact and disjoint from $\mathcal B_{c_b}$, there are $\eta_Q>0$ and $N_Q$ such that $$h\ge b_-+\eta_Q\quad\hbox{on }Q
 \label{n3:apriori:lower-height}$$ for every $N\ge N_Q$, every sufficiently large allowed truncation, and every admissible or floor-contact solution in those stages. If $Q$ is disjoint from $\mathcal W_{c_w}$, the analogous conclusion is $h\le b_+-\eta_Q$. The compact sets are relative to the full closure: they may contain faces of the opposite color.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-sublevels</summary>

*Proof.* We prove the lower assertion. It is enough to consider an arbitrary sequence $N_i\to\infty$, $R_i\to\infty$ and solutions in either of the first two stages. The elementary height and end estimates in Lemmas <a href="#n3:deformation:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:height">16</a> and <a href="#n3:deformation:end-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:end-height">17</a> give <a id="n3:apriori:elementary-height"></a>$$|h_i|\le C_0,\qquad
 |h_i|\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R_i^{-\gamma})\quad\hbox{on the end},
 \qquad 3/4<\gamma<1.
 \label{n3:apriori:elementary-height}$$ Near each white face extend $h_i$ to the other side by the constant $b_+$. Extend the fixed geometric coefficients smoothly there. The extended functions are continuous. Define the lower relaxed limit $$\underline h(x)=\lim_{j\to\infty}
       \inf\{h_i(y):i\ge j,\ \operatorname{dist}(x,y)<1/j\}.$$ It is lower semicontinuous, bounded, and satisfies the limiting end bound. No equicontinuity of $h_i$ is asserted.

Choose $b_-<k'<\min\{0,b_-+\eta\}$, where $\eta$ is the low-height sign range of the added term $D_0$. Suppose that a smooth function $\phi$ touches $\underline h$ from below at $x$, with $\underline h(x)\le k'$ and $d\phi(x)\ne0$. Exclude for the moment the black faces. Subtracting a small fourth-order localization term from $\phi$ makes the contact strict without changing its two-jet. Minimization on a small closed ball then produces, after passing to a subsequence, points $x_i\to x$ and constants $c_i\to0$ such that $\phi+c_i$ touches $h_i$ from below at $x_i$, and $h_i(x_i)\to\underline h(x)$. The boundary of this ball cannot contain $x_i$ by strictness. Nor can $x_i$ lie on a white face or on the extended side: their values there are $b_+>k'$. Thus every sufficiently large $i$ uses the interior trace equation.

<a id="n3:apriori:relaxed-test"></a>
At these contacts, $$\nabla f_i=\tau_i^{-1}\nabla\phi,
 \qquad
 d_i\le\frac{\tau_i^2}{\ell_i^2|d\phi(x_i)|^2}
          \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad a_i\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \chi_i\longrightarrow0.$$ Here $a_i=l_i|\nabla f_i|/\sqrt{D_i}$ is the deformation variable. Positivity of $A_{\chi_i}$ and the Hessian inequality at a lower contact imply $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_{\chi_i}}K+
 \frac{l_i}{\tau_i\sqrt{D_i}}
                 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_{\chi_i}}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi
 \le F_i(x_i).$$ In the second stage $D_0\le0$ at these values; in the first stage it is absent. Consequently $\limsup F_i(x_i)\le k'+C_b$. Passing to the limit gives $$\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\phi)^\perp}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi}{|d\phi|}
           +\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{(d\phi)^\perp}K\le k'+C_b.
 \label{n3:apriori:relaxed-test}$$ This is the expansion of the level surface of $\phi$, oriented toward increasing $\phi$. The only Hessian used in this passage is the fixed test Hessian. Removing the localization proves the assertion for non-strict contacts as well.

Fix $b_-<k<k'$ and put $E_k=\{\underline h\le k\}$. Apply Lemma <a href="#n3:apriori:sublevel-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:sublevel-support">21</a> with $u=\underline h$, tensor $Q=K$, and $q_0=k'+C_b$. The function is finite and lower semicontinuous, and Equation <a href="#n3:apriori:relaxed-test" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:relaxed-test">[n3:apriori:relaxed-test]</a> supplies the required bound for every nonzero-gradient lower test below $k'$. We apply the lemma locally away from black faces, using the constant extensions to obtain open neighborhoods across white faces. Every exterior support of $E_k$ there consequently has expansion at most $k'+C_b$, with no regularity assumption on the sublevel.

This argument also rules out a hidden layer at a white face. At every point strictly on the added side, the relaxed limit equals $b_+>k$. Thus $E_k$ lies locally in the original closed exterior, and the reversed white face is an exterior support of $E_k$ at any contact there, with expansion $$-H_B+P_B=-c_w>0.$$ For $k'$ sufficiently close to $b_-$, this is strictly greater than $k'+C_b$. The high extension ensured that all preceding low-value tests came from the interior equation, so the support contradiction applies at the face itself. Hence $E_k$ avoids every white face. The end estimate makes $E_k$ compact.

Adjoin the entire closed region $\mathcal B_{c_b}$. At a point on its smooth black frontier, every exterior support of the union also contains the black region locally. The tangency comparison therefore bounds its expansion by $c_b<k'+C_b$. At all other frontier points the preceding sublevel argument applies. The resulting compact closed set contains the required original inner barrier with a collar, because the black region already does. It avoids the outer barriers. Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">10</a> places it in a smooth black trapped region at any threshold $c''>k'+C_b$ sufficiently close to $c_b$. It is consequently contained in $\mathcal B_{c''}$.

Finally let $Q$ be as in the lemma. Hausdorff right continuity at $c_b$ gives a $\delta>0$ such that $\mathcal B_{c_b+\delta}\cap Q=\varnothing$; decrease $\delta$ so that the enlarged threshold is still negative and all barriers remain strict. Choose $k,k',c''$ with $$b_-<k<k',\qquad k'+C_b<c''<c_b+\delta.$$ The construction implies $E_k\cap Q=\varnothing$ for every sequence under consideration. If the uniform estimate $h>k$ on $Q$ failed, choose violating solutions with $N_i\to\infty$, $R_i\to\infty$ and $x_i\in Q$, $h_i(x_i)\le k$. A subsequence has $x_i\to x\in Q$ and $\underline h(x)\le k$, a contradiction. This gives <a href="#n3:apriori:lower-height" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:lower-height">[n3:apriori:lower-height]</a>, after decreasing its positive margin.

For the upper assertion apply the entire argument to $(-h,-K,-C)$, interchanging colors. The reversed black faces have strictly positive white expansion $-c_b$. Their exclusion and compactness give positive distance from the black region before applying the white version of Lemma <a href="#n3:domains:weak-support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:domains:weak-support">10</a>. Adjoining the full white region is therefore legitimate in the fixed black complement. Empty white regions and missing face types cause no change: only an actually nonempty sublevel would supply a trapped seed and hence a contradiction. ◻

</details>

For the truncation quantifier, start with any $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$ that satisfies the outer estimates of Section <a href="#n3:deformation:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:section">4</a>, and enlarge it when necessary. Failure of any asserted estimate for arbitrarily large $N$ and $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$ supplies exactly the sequence excluded above. Only finitely many compact sets will be needed below, so their thresholds can be chosen simultaneously.

The weak-set argument has kept low heights near black faces and high heights near white faces. We now sharpen this separation into a nonzero signed boundary slope. That slope makes the otherwise uncontrolled inner flux small enough for the mass estimate.

<a id="pm-h-25"></a>
#### Signed collar barriers

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-collars"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:collars" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:apriori:signed-slopes"></a>
**Lemma 23** (Boundary slopes). *There are fixed constants $c,C_*>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $N$ and the allowed truncations, the first two stages satisfy $$\begin{array}{ll}
 c/\tau\le\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on black faces},\\[2pt]
 c/\tau\le-\partial_\nu f\le C_*/\tau&\text{on white faces}.
 \end{array}
 \label{n3:apriori:signed-slopes}$$ During the third stage one still has $|\partial_\nu f|\le C_*/\tau$. On every fixed compact region needed for the final scalar-curvature estimate, the first two stages satisfy $b_-\le h\le b_+$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-collars"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-collars</summary>

<a id="n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy"></a>
*Proof.* Write $s$ for the smooth leaf parameter in an outward collar and $\nu_s=\nabla s/|ds|$. All geometric coefficients of this fixed collar are bounded, with $|ds|$ bounded above and below. At a comparison contact with $h_0=b_-+\psi(s)$, $\psi'>0$, the shared gradient gives $$d\le C\frac{\tau^2}{\ell^2(\psi')^2},\qquad
 1-a\le d,\qquad N\chi\ge c_1d\quad(N\ge4).
 \label{n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy}$$ If the slopes are in a fixed positive interval, the first bound is $d\le C\ell$. None of these comparisons uses an upper bound for $Z$.

<a id="n3:apriori:collar-trace"></a>
The trace operator on this test is $$\begin{aligned}
 &\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}\left(K+
       \frac{l}{\tau\sqrt D}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}h_0\right)\notag\\
 &\quad=P_s+aH_s+\chi K(\nu_s,\nu_s)
       +a\chi\left(
           \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}s(\nu_s,\nu_s)}{|ds|}
                      +|ds|\frac{\psi''}{\psi'}\right),
 \label{n3:apriori:collar-trace}
\end{aligned}$$ where $P_s$ is the tangential trace of $K$ on the leaf. Thus it is the leaf expansion $H_s+P_s$, with an error of absolute value at most $C d$, plus the displayed logarithmic-slope term. The same formula for a negative slope has $a$ replaced by $-a$ in the Hessian terms. This is an evaluation at the contact variables; it does not differentiate the unknown $t$.

<a id="n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual"></a>
On a black collar $H_s+P_s\ge c_b$ and $C=C_b-k_Bs$. Choose small positive slopes so that $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(s)\le k_Bs/2$. At the outer end of a sufficiently short fixed collar, Lemma <a href="#n3:apriori:sublevels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:sublevels">22</a> lets this test lie below the solution. In the compatible direction the add-on $D_0$ vanishes. The residual of the trace equation on the test is therefore at least $$k_Bs/2-Cd+a\chi|ds|\frac{\psi''}{\psi'}.
 \label{n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual}$$ Choose a smooth nonnegative $\beta_N(s)$ equal to $AN$ for $0\le s\le1/N$, supported in $0\le s\le2/N$, and satisfying $\int\beta_N\le2A$. Define $$\psi'(s)=m\exp\left(\int_0^s\beta_N(q)\,\mathrm dq\right).$$ Choose the fixed $A$ large enough that the final term of <a href="#n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual">[n3:apriori:lower-collar-residual]</a> dominates $Cd$ on $s\le1/N$, using <a href="#n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy">[n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy]</a> and $a\ge1/2$ there. On $s\ge1/N$, the first term dominates $Cd\le C\ell$ for large $N$; the taper contributes with the good sign. Since the slope multiplier is at most $e^{2A}$, a fixed sufficiently small $m>0$ enforces all the previous small-slope requirements. This constructs a strict lower barrier with slopes bounded above and below independently of $N$.

An upper barrier from $b_-$ is constructed in the same collar with $$\psi'(s)=M\exp\left(-\int_0^s\beta_N(q)\,\mathrm dq\right).$$ The smooth leaf expansion differs from its boundary value by $O(s)$. Choose the fixed $M$ so large that $\psi(s)\ge C_2s$ dominates this variation, the offset variation, and the height bound at the outer collar end. The logarithmic-slope term is now negative. On $s\le1/N$ it dominates $Cd$; on the rest of the collar the negative margin proportional to $s$ does so. The upper barrier is strict at every possible positive contact. Its slopes lie in $[Me^{-2A},M]$, an interval independent of $N$.

To check the comparison signs, at a negative interior minimum of $h-h_0$ the Hessian of $h$ dominates that of $h_0$, the gradients and $Z$ agree, and hence so do $t,l,A_\chi$. The right side is strictly increasing in the height. Thus a strict positive residual for a lower barrier contradicts the equation. At a positive maximum the inequalities reverse, proving the upper-barrier assertion. Taking the one-sided derivative at $s=0$ proves the black part of <a href="#n3:apriori:signed-slopes" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:signed-slopes">[n3:apriori:signed-slopes]</a>. Replacing $(h,K,C)$ by $(-h,-K,-C)$ proves the white part.

In the third stage the boundary height is the assigned interpolated constant, say $b_\zeta$. Construct tests $b_\zeta+\psi(s)$ and $b_\zeta-\psi(s)$ with large positive $\psi'$ and $(\log\psi')'=-\beta_N$. At $s=0$, the two directional inequalities of Proposition <a href="#n3:deformation:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:homotopy">15</a> say precisely that the positive-slope test has nonpositive limiting residual and the negative-slope test nonnegative limiting residual. At every comparison contact, the fixed positive barrier slope and Equation <a href="#n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy">[n3:apriori:contact-degeneracy]</a> give $d\le C\ell$, so $a\ge1/2$ for large $N$. On $1/2\le|w|\le1$, the first $w$-derivatives of $A_\chi$ in Equation <a href="#n3:deformation:axial-matrices" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:deformation:axial-matrices">[n3:deformation:axial-matrices]</a> are bounded independently of $0\le p\le N$. The other collar terms have fixed smooth coefficients on the bounded height range. Thus, at fixed boundary height the coefficient and geometric errors are $O(s+d+\chi)$, since $|w-(\pm\nu_s)|=1-a\le d$ and the radial comparison segment stays in this range. Changing the test height supplies, by height monotonicity, a residual of magnitude at least $\psi(s)$ with the required sign. Large fixed slopes dominate the $O(s)$ error and the outer-end height bound. The logarithmic-slope term has the required sign for both tests, as follows from <a href="#n3:apriori:collar-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:collar-trace">[n3:apriori:collar-trace]</a>; it dominates the $O(d)$ error on the initial $1/N$ interval. The remaining margin dominates it beyond that interval. This proves the two-sided upper derivative bound, without using sublevel exclusion in the third stage.

Finally, on each own-color collar the lower barrier just constructed gives the required one-sided height bound. On the rest of a fixed compact region use Lemma <a href="#n3:apriori:sublevels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:apriori:sublevels">22</a>; the opposite height bound on an own-color collar follows from that lemma as well, since the closed collar is disjoint from the other region. A finite cover proves $b_-\le h\le b_+$ on the compact regions in the statement. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-26"></a>
#### A trace estimate with polynomial constants

The collar trace estimate must have polynomial constants: it will control the boundary flux both here and in the mass estimate. We therefore prove it before comparing with the ordinary product graph.

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-trace"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:trace" class="lemma">

<a id="n3:apriori:weighted-trace"></a>
<a id="n3:apriori:unweighted-trace"></a>
**Lemma 24** (Weighted and unweighted collar traces). *In the first two stages let $\mathcal C$ be a fixed union of disjoint collars of the inner faces, shortened if necessary. For every nonnegative smooth function $\varphi$ supported in those collars, $$\begin{aligned}
 \int_B L\varphi\,\mathrm dA_g
 &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C}u
       \bigl[(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi
                          +|d\varphi|_{A_\chi}\bigr]\,\mathrm dV_g,
 \label{n3:apriori:weighted-trace}\\
 \int_B\varphi\,\mathrm dA_g
 &\le\Pi_N\int_{\mathcal C}\sqrt D
       \bigl[(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\varphi
                          +|d\varphi|_{A_\chi}\bigr]\,\mathrm dV_g.
 \label{n3:apriori:unweighted-trace}
\end{aligned}$$ The estimates also hold without a support condition on $\varphi$ if the right sides include a fixed collar cutoff equal to one on $B$, with its derivative included in the coefficient of $\varphi$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-trace"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-trace</summary>

<a id="n3:apriori:W-gradient"></a>
<a id="n3:apriori:W-divergence"></a>
<a id="n3:apriori:W-divergence-unweighted"></a>
*Proof.* For $\sigma>0$, write $e_f=\nabla f/\sigma$, the axis denoted by $e$ in Section <a href="#n3:deformation:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:section">4</a>. Set $$W=l\bar\nabla f=\frac{l\nabla f}{D}=\sqrt d\,a e_f.$$ Its norm in $\bar g$ is $a\le1$. For any covector $\xi$, $$|\xi(W)|\le |\xi|_{A_d}
                  \le\sqrt{1+N/4}\,|\xi|_{A_\chi}.
 \label{n3:apriori:W-gradient}$$ Direct differentiation, using $uW=Lw$, gives $$\begin{aligned}
 \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(uW)}u
 &=\sqrt d\left[
       \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_d}H^f+(dp+p_L)a\partial_{e_f}t\right],
 \label{n3:apriori:W-divergence}\\
 \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(\sqrt D\,W)}{\sqrt D}
 &=\sqrt d\left[
       \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_d}H^f+dp\,a\partial_{e_f}t\right].
 \label{n3:apriori:W-divergence-unweighted}
\end{aligned}$$ For example, $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}w=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_d}H^f+dp\,a\partial_{e_f}t$, while differentiating $L$ adds $p_La\partial_{e_f}t$ to the first formula. Coercivity in Lemma <a href="#n3:deformation:coercivity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:deformation:coercivity">13</a> bounds both right sides by $\Pi_N(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})$. More explicitly, writing $q=(K+H^f)_{e_fe_f}$, the normal Hessian term has coefficient $d^{3/2}$, so it is bounded by $\sqrt d|q|+C$. The other Hessian terms are transverse traces, and the gradient term is at most $(2N+2)\sqrt d|\partial_{e_f}t|$. All are controlled by the stated coercivity estimate. This also establishes the formulas and bounds at zero gradient by their smooth direction-free extensions.

Let $\varepsilon_B=1$ on a black collar and $-1$ on a white collar. The signed slopes give $w_\nu=\varepsilon_B a$ on $B$ and $a\ge1/2$ for large $N$. Thus $$uW_\nu=\varepsilon_B La,
 \qquad \sqrt D\,W_\nu=\varepsilon_B a.$$ The outward integration normal is $-\nu$. Apply the divergence theorem to $-\varepsilon_B uW\varphi$, with a fixed collar cutoff. Its boundary flux is $La\varphi$. Equations <a href="#n3:apriori:W-gradient" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:W-gradient">[n3:apriori:W-gradient]</a> and <a href="#n3:apriori:W-divergence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:W-divergence">[n3:apriori:W-divergence]</a>, and the fixed cutoff derivative, give <a href="#n3:apriori:weighted-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:weighted-trace">[n3:apriori:weighted-trace]</a>. Replace $u$ by $\sqrt D$ and use <a href="#n3:apriori:W-divergence-unweighted" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:W-divergence-unweighted">[n3:apriori:W-divergence-unweighted]</a> for <a href="#n3:apriori:unweighted-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:unweighted-trace">[n3:apriori:unweighted-trace]</a>. No factor $\ell^{-1}$ was used. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-27"></a>
#### High-level energy and the first upper bound

<a id="n3:apriori:high-source"></a>
The signed slopes and polynomial trace estimate are now available. We use them before allowing any constants that depend arbitrarily on $N$. The first stage contains the drift in the divergence equation. We first bound this stage uniformly for $\lambda\in[0,1]$. There is a number $M_0=M_0(N)>0$ such that $$\Xi\ge\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+
                      \tfrac12\delta_0\tau a\sigma
          \quad\hbox{on }\{Z>M_0\}.
 \label{n3:apriori:high-source}$$ Indeed, outside the support of $m_0$ this is immediate. On its support, $-\epsilon\le t\le-\epsilon+1/N$, so $l$ is comparable to $\ell$. The identity $D=e^{8(Z-t)}$ shows that $a\sigma$ tends uniformly to infinity as $Z\to\infty$ in that band. The penalty $\mathcal P$ is bounded on the whole exterior by $\Pi_N$. It is therefore absorbed by $\delta_0\tau a\sigma/2$ above a fixed $M_0(N)$. This choice is independent of $R$ and $\lambda$.

Choose a smooth nondecreasing $k_0$ equal to zero on $Z\le M_0$, equal to one on $Z\ge M_0+1$, and with bounded derivative. Test $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}V_\lambda=u\Xi$ by $k_0(Z)$. Its outer boundary term vanishes since $Z=0$. The drift cross term is bounded by $$u k_0'\left|\langle dZ,K(w,\cdot)\rangle_{A_\chi}\right|
 \le 2u k_0'|dZ|_{A_\chi}^2+C u k_0'|K|^2.$$ The last term has bounded integral: it is supported on a fixed compact set and on $M_0\le Z\le M_0+1$, where the floor and $D=e^{8(Z-t)}$ bound $u$ and $\sigma$ by $C(N)$.

<a id="n3:apriori:small-boundary-flux"></a>
<a id="n3:apriori:high-energy-before-trace"></a>
At a black face $F-P_B=H$, $w_\nu=a$; at a white face $F-P_B=-H$, $w_\nu=-a$. In both cases $$-H+w_\nu(F-P_B)=(a-1)H.$$ The additional omitted-drift term in the homotopy boundary condition has absolute value at most $C\chi\le Cd$, since $A_\chi K(w,\cdot)$ has normal component $\chi w_\nu K(\nu,\nu)$. The remaining term is $-N_Bd$, and the boundary multiplier lies between zero and one. Hence $$|(V_\lambda)_\nu|\le Cud=CL\sqrt d
                       \le C\frac\tau\ell L\quad\hbox{on }B,
 \label{n3:apriori:small-boundary-flux}$$ where the last inequality uses the lower slope in <a href="#n3:apriori:signed-slopes" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:signed-slopes">[n3:apriori:signed-slopes]</a>. Integration now gives $$\begin{aligned}
 &\int_{\Omega_R}u k_0
       \left(\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+
                      \tfrac12\delta_0\tau a\sigma\right)\,\mathrm dV_g
       +2\int_{\Omega_R}u k_0'|dZ|_{A_\chi}^2\,\mathrm dV_g\notag\\
 &\hspace{18mm}\le C(N)+C\frac\tau\ell
                                  \int_B Lk_0\,\mathrm dA_g.
 \label{n3:apriori:high-energy-before-trace}
\end{aligned}$$

<a id="n3:apriori:high-energy"></a>
Apply <a href="#n3:apriori:weighted-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:weighted-trace">[n3:apriori:weighted-trace]</a> with the fixed collar cutoff. The boundary cost is at most $$\Pi_N\frac\tau\ell\int_{\mathcal C}u
       \left[k_0(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})
                              +k_0'|dZ|_{A_\chi}\right]\,\mathrm dV_g.$$ Let $\rho_{\mathcal C}>0$ be the minimum of $\rho$ on the closed collars. Pointwise, $1+\sqrt{\mathcal T}\le C(\rho+\delta_0\mathcal T)$ there, with $C$ fixed. Since $\Pi_N\tau/\ell\to0$, the first summand is absorbed in the first integral of <a href="#n3:apriori:high-energy-before-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:high-energy-before-trace">[n3:apriori:high-energy-before-trace]</a>. Young’s inequality bounds the derivative summand by $$u k_0'|dZ|_{A_\chi}^2+
          C(\Pi_N\tau/\ell)^2u k_0'.$$ The second term again has bounded compact integral because it lies in the transition strip of $k_0$. We obtain $$\int u k_0(\mathcal T+\rho+\tau a\sigma)\,\mathrm dV_g
       +\int u k_0'|dZ|_{A_\chi}^2\,\mathrm dV_g\le C(N).
 \label{n3:apriori:high-energy}$$ The smallness requirement on $N$ in this absorption is independent of $M_0$; only its resulting right-hand constant depends on $M_0$.

<a id="n3:apriori:L2"></a>
The polynomial boundary absorption is complete. We may now use arbitrary fixed-$N$ comparison constants. Write $\Gamma$ for the ordinary product graph of $f$ in $g+(\,\mathrm db_0)^2$, and $\,\mathrm d\Gamma=\sqrt{1+\sigma^2}\,\mathrm dV_g$. The measures $\,\mathrm d\Gamma$ and $\sqrt D\,\mathrm dV_g$ are comparable by constants depending only on $\ell$. On every fixed compact set $Q$, $$\int_{\Gamma\cap\pi^{-1}(Q)}e^{2Z}\,\mathrm d\Gamma\le C_Q(N),
 \label{n3:apriori:L2}$$ where $\pi$ is projection to the base. To check this without an upper bound for $t$, observe that $$e^{2Z}=e^{2t}D^{1/4},\qquad u=le^{2t}\sqrt D,
 \qquad D^{1/4}\le C(N)(1+\tau a\sigma).$$ The last inequality follows by splitting $l\sigma\le1$ and $l\sigma>1$, using $\ell\le l\le e$; on the second set $a\ge1/\sqrt2$ and the right side grows linearly in $\sigma$, whereas $D^{1/4}$ grows at most as $C\sqrt\sigma$. Thus the high-level part of <a href="#n3:apriori:L2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:L2">[n3:apriori:L2]</a> follows from <a href="#n3:apriori:high-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:high-energy">[n3:apriori:high-energy]</a> and the positive minimum of $\rho$ on $Q$. On $Z\le M_0+1$, both $\sigma$ and $e^{2Z}$ are bounded by the floor identity, which controls the remaining compact integral.

<a id="pm-h-28"></a>
#### Sobolev inequality and iteration on the ordinary graph

The high-level estimate gives integral control, but degree requires a pointwise upper bound for $Z$. The graph Sobolev inequality and iteration supply that bound. The earlier polynomial trace estimate, not the constants in this iteration, will control the mass limit.

The comparisons in this subsection are uniform in the solution, $R$, and the homotopy parameter, but may depend arbitrarily on $N$. If $d_0=(1+\sigma^2)^{-1}$, then $$|d\varphi|_{A_{d_0}}=|\nabla_\Gamma\varphi|,
 \qquad
 \frac{d}{d_0}=\frac{1+\sigma^2}{1+l^2\sigma^2}.$$ The last ratio is bounded above and below by constants depending only on $\ell$; Equation <a href="#n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons">[n3:apriori:parameter-comparisons]</a> therefore compares $A_{d_0},A_d,A_\chi$ without any bound for $Z$.

<a id="stmt-n3-apriori-sobolev"></a>
<div id="n3:apriori:sobolev" class="lemma">

**Lemma 25** (Local graph Sobolev inequality). *For a smooth function $\omega$ supported over a fixed compact base patch, which may meet an inner face, <a id="n3:apriori:sobolev-equation"></a>$$\|\omega\|_{L^6(\,\mathrm d\Gamma)}^2
 \le C(N)\int_\Gamma
       \left[|\nabla_\Gamma\omega|^2+
                            (1+\mathcal T)\omega^2\right]\,\mathrm d\Gamma.
 \label{n3:apriori:sobolev-equation}$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n3-apriori-sobolev"><summary>Proof of stmt-n3-apriori-sobolev</summary>

*Proof.* Extend the fixed base patch smoothly and embed a compact enlargement isometrically in Euclidean space by Nash’s embedding theorem (Nash 1956, Theorem 2, p. 59) <a id="pm-cite-42"></a>[[Nash1956](#ref-Nash1956)]. Its product with the vertical line gives an isometric Euclidean immersion of the graph. The second fundamental form of the base embedding is bounded, so its contribution to the graph mean curvature vector is bounded. The scalar mean curvature in the product is $$H_\Gamma=
 \frac{\sqrt D}{l\sqrt{1+\sigma^2}}
       \left(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{e_f^\perp}H^f+d_0H^f(e_f,e_f)\right).$$ The prefactor is bounded by $C(N)$, and $d_0/\sqrt d=\sqrt{1+l^2\sigma^2}/(1+\sigma^2)\le e$. Coercivity therefore gives $|\boldsymbol H_\Gamma|\le C(N)(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})$. This estimate involves controlled quadratic energy, not a pointwise bound for the Hessian.

The ordinary Michael–Simon inequality (Michael and Simon 1973) <a id="pm-cite-43"></a>[[MichaelSimon1973](#ref-MichaelSimon1973)], in the compact-support form stated in (Simon 2014, chap. 4, Section 5, Theorem 5.7, p. 98) <a id="pm-cite-44"></a>[[Simon2014](#ref-Simon2014)], gives after the boundary extension described below, for nonnegative $\varphi$, $$\left(\int_\Gamma\varphi^{3/2}\,\mathrm d\Gamma\right)^{2/3}
 \le C\left[
       \int_\Gamma(|\nabla_\Gamma\varphi|
